comments.text:
Reference gate (pre-implementation, 2026-08-04)

Identities inspected:
- libghostty-vt =0.2.1 and libghostty-vt-sys =0.2.1 from the local Cargo registry; the sys crate pins Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083.
- Ghostty source at a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083.
- Ghostling at f9034e43a50a2f3a8101e35497f486090c1ddd6e.
- libghostty-rs at 72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6.
- justerm at 0e468a7fde4e75d307983258d09dd8dfbe26f81a.
- zmx attach-ordering audit at 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4.
- orb-bi4.1 Formatter counterexamples in tests/formatter_attachment.rs and README.md.

Mechanisms accepted:
- libghostty-vt RenderState::update(&Terminal) is the sole authoritative presentation snapshot boundary. Its Snapshot/row/cell iterators expose viewport geometry, graphemes, styles, resolved colors, cursor state, palette/default colors, and selection; Terminal::grid_ref exposes hyperlink URIs; Terminal exposes title, working directory, active screen, and Kitty graphics state.
- Ghostling and libghostty-rs confirm the intended ownership/lifetime pattern: update one RenderState from the authoritative Terminal, then render/read only that snapshot. Orbit will use the published safe crate rather than copy either reference.
- justerm confirms that transport should carry a versioned, self-contained structured frame and keep transport consumer-owned. Its damage protocol is deliberately not adopted for this first proof.
- zmx confirms the ordering hazard: already-readable PTY input must be consumed into terminal authority before choosing an attach snapshot; the initial frame must be queued before any later revision. Orbit remains the sole terminal-response owner.

Mechanisms rejected for this slice:
- Formatter checkpoints, raw-PTY tails, client-side terminal emulation, unbounded replay, speculative delta/damage protocols, multiple clients, renderer/window/input stacks, Zellij compatibility, and copied/forked bindings.
- zmx's raw-byte broadcast, multi-client buffers, query-ownership switching, and formatter restoration workarounds.
- justerm's broader version-14 scroll/damage/selection/marker/search framework.

Consequence for implementation:
- The public libghostty-vt API is sufficient; no binding extension, fork, second terminal engine, or decision gate is needed.
- Keep the current single package/binary. Add at most one focused presentation module. Use complete host-authored frames with an Orbit monotonic revision; preserve ordered delivery by holding at most the in-flight frame plus one replaceable latest frame for a slow nonblocking client.
- Rich text/cursor/color/title/cwd/screen/hyperlink state will be represented. Kitty graphics will be explicitly declared unsupported in this first wire capability instead of being silently lost; public graphics access remains available for a later user-chosen slice.

Crate decision (no new-crate gate triggered):
- Existing pinned libc and libghostty-vt are sufficient. A small deterministic encoder and bounded queue are cheaper than serde/bincode/bytes/tokio or another terminal crate, so Cargo.toml and the normal dependency tree remain unchanged.

Cheapest first check:
- A real PTY emits state before attach and again while attaching. The client must decode one complete frame at revision N followed only by higher revisions; the final decoded frame must equal a fresh frame from Orbit's authoritative terminal. The fixture also covers styled/color text, cursor state, title/cwd, alternate-screen state, a hyperlink, wide/combining graphemes, and an explicit graphics capability. No raw PTY byte or Formatter reconstruction is accepted.

Portability/architecture effect:
- Presentation extraction is platform-neutral Rust above the existing Linux PTY seam. This slice does not widen the Linux-first boundary or touch PTY backend ownership.

Candidate evidence / closure gate pending user acceptance (2026-08-04)

Outcome:
- The real PTY remains owned by the existing single-threaded authoritative loop. Every PTY drain mutates the sole libghostty Terminal, advances one monotonic Orbit revision, extracts one complete RenderState snapshot, and publishes it without raw PTY bytes.
- The first accepted-client bytes are FRAME <length> plus a version-1 ORBF payload at the current revision. That initial message is non-coalescible; later adjacent unsent complete frames coalesce to the newest revision while a partially sent frame remains intact.
- Version 1 carries dimensions, active screen, title, working directory, default colors, cursor color, the 256-color palette, cursor visibility/blink/password/style/viewport, row wrap flags, every viewport cell's grapheme, wide role, full style colors/flags/underline, selection/protection, and hyperlink URI. It advertises hyperlinks and explicitly declares Kitty graphics unsupported.
- Frames are limited to 4 MiB and 100,000 cells. Nonblocking output has a fixed approximately 8 MiB aggregate bound; the slow-client proof drives 1.6 MiB through the PTY while the client stops reading, then reattaches and observes the final state.
- Semantic input and terminal-generated PTY responses remain authoritative in Orbit. No Formatter state, raw PTY tail, second emulator, replay log, damage protocol, fork, binding extension, platform edit, graphical code, or extra session/client scope was added.

- First check was made red before implementation: cargo test --test lifecycle shell_survives_detach_and_one_client_reattaches -- --exact failed because attachment still began with ATTACHED rather than FRAME.

- A deterministic queue check proves the initial frame is retained and adjacent pending frames retain only the latest revision.

All hardening descendants are complete. Host-owned history remains the separate orb-j0m frontier before Eon dogfood and graduation.

1. orb-bi4.5.1 bounds canonical transport corruption and pressure in Orbit.
2. orb-bi4.5.2 closes Orbit attachment and process-lifecycle races.
3. orb-bi4.5.3 contains three children for parser/reply authority, semantic input/resize, and rich presentation fidelity.
4. orb-bi4.5.4 measures the accepted Orbit-Venus pair under real workloads without product edits.

Each implementation task owns one Orbit failure domain, records its own Execution baseline and Reference gate, and updates the exact ORB-C proofs it touches. Any Venus correction is a separate Venus-owned Bead and commit. The final child consumes proofs and routes defects; it does not repair them. Close this parent only after every descendant and the contract indexes agree.

1. orb-bi4.4 accepts and records the exact Orbit and Venus boundary before orb-bi4.5.1 begins.
2. orb-bi4.5.1 proves bounded canonical transport behavior under malformed input, rapid output, slow readers, and failed delivery.
3. orb-bi4.5.2 proves bounded, idempotent attachment, child, signal, shutdown, and socket lifecycle behavior.
4. orb-bi4.5.3.1, orb-bi4.5.3.2, and orb-bi4.5.3.3 separately prove parser and reply authority, semantic input and resize, and rich presentation fidelity; orb-bi4.5.3 reconciles and closes their accepted evidence.

6. Every correction has one repository owner. Cross-repository changes use separate Beads and commits with exact compatibility and update order.
7. ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 are advanced to exact accepted proof revisions or explicitly downgraded with remaining gaps; preserved contracts rerun their indexed checks.
8. Closure records portability, dependencies, owned LOC, exact checks, measurements, the performance decision, and rejected or deferred fuzzing.

10. Host-owned history, native scrolling, selection, and copy remain outside this hardening epic and proceed only through orb-j0m after closure. Search remains separate in orb-qcc.
11. Patches, effects, graphics resources, dirty-row extraction, remote transport, restart persistence, workspace topology, and multiplayer remain separate user decisions.

title: Bound the one-client transport under corruption and pressure
description:
Contract routing:
- Hardens ORB-C3, ORB-C4, and ORB-C7.
- Preserves ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C5, and ORB-C6.
- Changes no product feature or compatibility boundary unless the user separately approves it.

Prove the Orbit-owned canonical session and frame transport remains bounded and convergent under malformed input, rapid PTY output, a client that stops reading, and failed frame delivery. This Bead owns Orbit production and protocol checks only. A Venus defect is reported to Venus and is not fixed in the same run.
design:
Begin only after orb-bi4.4 accepts the exact Venus consumer. Record the Execution baseline and pass the Reference gate before code.

Required before code: exact routed zmx source behavior for slow clients and attachment ordering; FrankenTerm transport and bounded-failure mechanisms; and FrankenTUI deterministic transition and headless-check mechanisms. Foot 1.27.0 at de998602dbc00c8862a6823d553cbb1df91c676d is comparison only. Accept failure cases and test mechanisms, not another multiplexer, TUI stack, or terminal authority.

Use the existing canonical codecs, bounded queues, and owned synchronous loop. Start with deterministic malformed, truncated, oversized, allocation-hostile, stale, and reordered message checks plus a sustained slow-reader case. cargo-fuzz remains conditional on a named decoder risk that focused checks cannot cover economically; activating it requires its own Crate gate and user approval. Stop for a protocol revision, new dependency, event-loop replacement, or cross-repository correction.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Malformed, truncated, oversized, unsupported, stale, and reordered client input or frame state fails deterministically before unbounded allocation or retained storage.
2. Rapid PTY output and a client that stops reading cannot block authoritative PTY processing indefinitely or grow queues or frame history without bound.
3. Coalescing preserves a coherent latest complete frame with no duplicate, regressing, or missing final revision.
4. Client failure releases unread and retained transport storage and does not admit later input or frame publication.
5. Checks use explicit synchronization, bounded timeouts, and the canonical Orbit representation; redundant implementation-trivia checks are removed.
6. Orbit is the sole code owner in this Bead. Any Venus defect or boundary change is routed separately with exact revisions and compatibility order.
7. Closure reruns and updates or explicitly downgrades every touched ORB-C3, ORB-C4, and ORB-C7 proof and regression-checks preserved contracts.
8. Closure records the portability disposition, dependency and fuzz disposition, owned LOC, measurements, exact commands, and remaining pressure limits. Patches, dirty-row extraction, history, effects, resources, remote transport, and multiplayer remain excluded.
notes: Accepted proof fdd55e1e8bf6b932c2949ea3c897601ff63c0743. Orbit keeps one synchronous owner loop, sole libghostty authority, canonical ORBS/ORBF codecs, existing OutputQueue, and the isolated Linux platform seam. The loop processes one 8192-byte PTY read per readiness turn. Terminal replies and semantic input share one ordered 1,048,592-byte backlog; input pressure rejects the whole new semantic message with a terminal failure and closes that client, while reply overflow terminates the session rather than losing an authoritative response. The canonical real-PTY proof sends 4 MiB to a non-reading client, interrupts a continuously emitting child through semantic Ctrl-C, and converges on the final complete frame after reattach within five-second synchronization bounds. ORB-C3 and ORB-C4 are hardened; ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C5, and ORB-C6 are preserved; ORB-C7 remains partial only for lifecycle races and cleanup in orb-bi4.5.2. No manifest, dependency, feature, transitive graph, protocol, or Venus change occurred. cargo-fuzz remains unnecessary because focused canonical checks cover truncation, malformed and allocation-hostile declarations, unsupported versions, and stale or reordered frames. Product Rust is 5,746 lines, net +101; governance Rust remains 765. Portability is neutral above the unchanged isolated Linux platform dependency. Exact accepted checks: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace with 45 tests; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; Starcompass check-consumer; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Rejected: runtime replacement, new crate, protocol revision, patches, history, effects, resources, remote transport, multiplayer, public trace, and cross-repository correction. Remaining limits are one local client and session, complete frames, no restart persistence, and terminal failure if reply production exceeds the fixed backlog.
close_reason: Accepted bounded one-client transport pressure proof at fdd55e1e8bf6b932c2949ea3c897601ff63c0743.

title: Close attachment and process lifecycle races
description:
Contract routing:
- Hardens ORB-C1, ORB-C3, and ORB-C7.
- Preserves ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, and ORB-C6.
- Changes no product feature or compatibility boundary unless the user separately approves it.

Prove that attach, detach, client failure, child exit, server shutdown, signals, and socket cleanup have one bounded, idempotent Orbit owner. This Bead changes Orbit only; consumer UX findings are routed to Venus separately.
design:
Run after the transport-pressure child. Record the Execution baseline and pass the Reference gate before code.

Required before code: exact FrankenTerm session, reconnect, crash, and cleanup mechanisms; Process Triage observe-plan-apply, staged signal, reaping, and post-action verification mechanisms; zmx attach-ordering and restoration failures; and Qwertty raw-mode restoration and cleanup mechanisms. Foot 1.27.0 at de998602dbc00c8862a6823d553cbb1df91c676d is comparison only. Reject their remote, multi-session, controlling-terminal, fleet, and general cleanup scope.

Exercise aborted and simultaneous handshakes, deterministic second-client rejection, client crash, detached resize ownership, PTY EOF, foreground and known-child exit, server shutdown, signals, stale socket identity, and repeated cleanup. Use the existing platform seam and owned loop. Stop for a new process model, restart persistence, remote transport, new crate, or cross-repository correction.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Aborted, raced, and simultaneous attachment attempts preserve exactly one active client; rejection does not disturb the accepted client or PTY.
2. Client disconnect or crash leaves the live PTY/session available for coherent reattachment while Orbit remains running.
3. PTY EOF, foreground or known-child exit, server shutdown, and supported signals drain or discard owned state according to the indexed contracts without hangs or duplicate terminal actions.
4. Socket and platform resources are cleaned idempotently; stale identity cannot remove another listener or admit an unintended attachment.
5. Slow or failed lifecycle transitions use explicit synchronization and bounded timeouts and leave no abandoned client storage.
6. Orbit is the sole code owner in this Bead. Any Venus UX defect or boundary change is routed separately with exact revisions and compatibility order.
7. Closure reruns and updates or explicitly downgrades every touched ORB-C1, ORB-C3, and ORB-C7 proof and regression-checks preserved contracts.
8. Closure records portability, dependency footprint, owned LOC, exact verification, and remaining lifecycle limits. Restart persistence, multiple sessions, remote transport, and multiplayer remain excluded.
notes:
Accepted ownership: the one Orbit owner loop handles known-child exit by invoking the existing Pty cleanup owner before bounded final PTY materialization. Pty holds the live child as Option<Child>; cleanup takes Some to None before signaling and reaping, so later explicit or Drop cleanup is a no-op without an independent stopped flag. Cleanup always signals the owned child process group and any distinct foreground process group even after the leader exits, then kills and reaps the exact known child. Drop remains the fallback on other exits. Steady-state remains one PTY read per readiness turn.

After quiescence, Orbit consumes at most four PTY-master reads and stops earlier on closed/WouldBlock. The zmx measured Linux N_TTY maximum bounds this near 16 KiB. The real-PTY final-state regression emits 5,000 padding bytes before its final OSC title, requiring multiple reads and proving the reproduced final state reaches authoritative libghostty. The continuously writing inherited-PTY descendant regression proves bounded server exit, socket removal, and descendant cleanup. Excess raw output beyond the four-read post-exit budget is deliberately discarded when Pty drops; no client can attach after Exited.

Material rejected exit shapes: one final read lost the title; FIONREAD exposed only the current 4,095-byte chunk and missed later asynchronous PTY transfer; 4 MiB and 64 KiB drain caps let a live producer exceed the lifecycle deadline; stopping process groups followed by an unbounded finite-tail drain still flaked when debug libghostty materialization exceeded five seconds. Quiescence plus the deterministic four-read budget is the smallest shape that preserves the reproduced multi-read final state and the hard shutdown bound. A separate stopped boolean was rejected because Option<Child> directly represents whether cleanup ownership remains.

ORB-C3 negotiation, invalid ordering, simultaneous rejection, abort recovery, and canonical reattachment share one strong lifecycle test. Client holds negotiation_deadline: Option<Instant>; Some means awaiting Hello until the existing one-second deadline and None means attached. This removes the independent attached/timestamp invariant. Other peers receive Busy while negotiation is live; expiry closes the abandoned socket and releases the slot without disturbing the PTY. The canonical validation client retries Unix-socket I/O and pre-attachment Busy responses within its existing five-second deadline. Canonical decode and ordering errors fail immediately: Attached is accepted exactly once, and duplicate Attached or Busy after Attached is rejected. Unbounded reservation, newest-peer eviction, duplicated server attached state, client-side ownership, a timer thread, and an async/state-machine framework were rejected.

The real-PTY detach proof observes PTY resize through the shell title and asserts retained 100x40 dimensions on the reattached client coherent initial frame. Shell PID continuity, deterministic Busy rejection, detached command completion, and owned cleanup remain co-located.

No wire protocol, dependency, manifest, platform abstraction, product boundary, timeout value, or attached-client behavior changes. Product Rust is 5,810 LOC, 64 lines over the prior accepted state. Portability disposition: neutral lifecycle, negotiation-deadline, and quiescence policy with Linux process groups, signals, PTY EOF, poll, and Unix sockets retained in the existing concrete platform seam.

Accepted proof revision 9e9b136969dc583d365daa75402ec03c265080f1 is compatible lifecycle hardening: ORBS v1, ORBF v1, orbit-protocol, manifests, dependencies, and valid client behavior are unchanged, so Venus requires no migration. Exact clean detached Linux verification at that revision passed cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; source-independent Starcompass consumer validation; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; commit diff checking; and clean-worktree checking. The focused attachment negotiation and race check also passed independently. docs/CONTRACTS.md advances preserved ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, and ORB-C6 plus hardened ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 to that revision and proves ORB-C7 for the accepted local one-client boundary.

The real-PTY proof makes previously unobservable mappings fail visibly. Shift+Enter release produces exact ESC [ 13 ; 2 : 3 u under authoritative Kitty mode. The q event carries active-and-consumed Alt yet remains plain q, proving consumed modifiers reach libghostty without changing unrelated text events. The enabled SGR left press carries Shift and uses surface pixel 915,725 in the bottom-right padding of a 920x740 surface with 9x17 cells, 10px horizontal padding, and 30px vertical padding. Ghostty must derive the 100x40 grid, subtract top and left padding, clamp to its final cell, and emit exact one-based cell 100,40. Every screen, cell, and padding field participates in the report boundary or coordinate result.

title: Measure the accepted Orbit-Venus boundary under real workloads
description: This is the final no-code acceptance slice for orb-bi4.5. It changes no product contract. Consume the exact accepted Orbit and Venus proofs and measure the real one-client boundary under representative terminal workloads. Route every confirmed defect to its single owning repository and Bead instead of repairing it inside this measurement run.
design:
Run only after transport pressure, lifecycle, and terminal-semantic hardening close. Pin the exact ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 proof revisions being exercised.

Before the first workload run, record the exact machine, display stack, window and grid size, commands, sampling method, and explicit numeric pass/fail ceilings. The envelope must cover p50 and p95 input-to-present latency when externally observable, idle CPU and RSS, sustained-output CPU and RSS, extraction time, encoded bytes per frame and per second, queue replacement, Venus apply or rebuild time, resize-storm convergence, and final-state convergence. A metric that cannot be observed without production instrumentation is marked unavailable before the run; do not silently replace it with an internal proxy.

Dogfood an ordinary shell, Neovim, Yazi, resize storms, and high-volume output. Use existing diagnostics or external observation. If meaningful measurement needs production instrumentation, a public trace, an adapter, or a dependency, stop and route that capability separately.

The result makes one decision. If the predeclared envelope passes, accept complete ORBF frames for the pre-graduation dogfood path and retain snapshots as the resynchronization fallback. If it fails, identify the limiting stage and route one owner correction; propose dirty-row extraction or snapshot-plus-row-patch only when extraction, encoding, transfer, or complete-scene application is the measured limit. This task may append factual evidence and update planning or contract documentation after accepted proofs, but it must not edit Orbit or Venus production code, tests, or manifests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before measurement, record the exact Orbit and Venus proof revisions, consumed contract IDs, machine and display environment, workload commands, observation method, and numeric pass/fail ceilings.
2. The declared envelope covers p50 and p95 input-to-present latency when externally observable, idle CPU and RSS, sustained-output CPU and RSS, extraction time, encoded bytes per frame and per second, queue replacement, Venus apply or rebuild time, resize convergence, and final-state convergence. Unobservable metrics are declared before the run with the missing observation surface.
3. Shell, Neovim, Yazi, resize-storm, and high-volume-output runs record the declared measurements against identical named conditions rather than incomparable anecdotes.
4. Detach, client loss, and reattachment preserve coherent current state during representative workloads and expose bounded visible failure behavior.
5. The result states one evidence-backed outcome: complete frames pass the envelope for pre-graduation dogfood, or the boundary is a no-go pending one routed owner correction. Passing does not claim that patches are never needed.
6. A failed metric identifies the limiting stage before proposing a remedy. Dirty-row extraction or snapshot-plus-row-patch is proposed only when measured extraction, encoding, transfer, or complete-scene application cost is causal.
7. Measurements distinguish observed facts from inference and do not promote visible-only dogfood into history, effects, graphics, platform, or restart-persistence proof.
8. Every confirmed defect is routed to one owning Orbit or Venus Bead with compatibility order where needed; no production code, test, manifest, adapter, dependency, or new trace surface changes here.
9. The result records the still-separate history and ordered-effect gaps. orb-bi4.5 reconciles the accepted child proofs, measurements, decision, and remaining risks before closure.
10. orb-bi4.6 remains blocked until this task and orb-bi4.5 close.
notes: Measured no-go at Orbit 847cab1 and Venus 8149002. All declared functional and lifecycle workloads passed, but sustained output exceeded the combined CPU ceiling: p95 240 percent versus 200 percent. External attribution was Orbit 101 percent and Venus 141 percent p95. Routed one Venus-only correction as ven-39u. Complete frames and ORBS v1 remain accepted contracts but are not accepted for pre-graduation dogfood until the correction passes this exact envelope. History orb-j0m, ordered effects orb-ll1, and graphics orb-j2i remain separate.
close_reason: Measurement complete: sustained-output CPU is a no-go at combined p95 240 percent versus the 200 percent ceiling; routed the single owner correction to Venus Bead ven-39u.

Disconnect or exit Venus while the agent task remains active; verify Orbit, the PTY and agent process survive; reattach coherently; continue user interaction; and observe a completion or failure.

This pre-graduation agent workload does not require an Eon AgentRun model. It must distinguish authoritative process/terminal lifecycle from semantic agent state. Compare the pair with the current Nova Mars and Zellij path on identical named conditions. Inspect exact current Herdr and VS Code Agent Host mechanisms as comparison evidence for client-independent agent work, not as dependencies or inherited feature scope. Record friction against the owning contract rather than widening Orbit, Venus or Eon.

Separate repositories remain deliberate boundaries whose coordination cost is measured at graduation.

title: Choose post-graduation Eon, Venus, and Orbit ownership boundaries
description:
After a go in orb-bi4.8, choose exactly one post-graduation implementation frontier and its cross-repository order. Preserve Orbit as generic terminal-session authority, Venus as native materializer and interaction owner, and Eon as agent-first workspace, product policy, orchestration, composition and distribution owner. On a no-go, close this Bead as not applicable.

Product direction:
Agents are strategically central to Eon. The user selected eon-pxn as the single post-graduation implementation frontier: an Eon-owned workspace model that treats AgentRun as explicit product identity and maps it to repositories or worktrees, provider identities, services, artifacts, execution targets and independent Orbit sessions. Its user-selected first native topology is a fixed two-axis surface: horizontal tabs and a visual vertical accordion pane stack with direct directional traversal and no virtual pane picker. This decision establishes ownership and order without activating implementation or another frontier.

Narrow-waist rule:
1. Keep an agent independent from a pane, PTY, process, Orbit session, provider thread and Venus view.
2. Keep process and terminal truth in Orbit, provider-native semantic evidence in an explicit integration, normalized AgentRun and attention policy in Eon, and native presentation in Venus.
3. For cross-boundary behavior compare no protocol change, an existing bounded plane and the smallest explicit extension in that order.
4. Keep snapshots or patches, history, effects, resources, actions, agent observation and product control as distinct responsibilities.
5. Every extension names one benefit, owner, consumer, numeric bounds, authorization, cancellation, compatibility, portability, proof and total LOC/runtime cost.
6. Keep exact-revision lockstep while Orbit and Venus are the only accepted pair. Add no public protocol, shared schema repository, compatibility window, generalized negotiation, plugin ABI or provider framework without an independently approved need.
7. Accept one vertical slice before another. Reopen architecture rather than accumulate adapters when coordination or duplicated truth becomes disproportionate.
design:
Current ownership:
- Orbit owns PTYs, terminal state, terminal viewport, selection, copy text, process/session lifetime and generic terminal identity.
- Venus owns frame materialization, native gesture collection, window geometry, focus, accessibility and platform clipboard or launch side effects. It owns no terminal viewport or history truth.
- Eon owns workspace topology and product policy: repositories or worktrees, AgentRuns, services, artifacts, execution-target references, launch and resume policy, secrets policy, component relationships and mappings to Orbit session identities.

Agent state remains source-aware. Orbit can prove process/session lifecycle, not provider intent. Provider semantic state is accepted only from an explicit integration. Eon may compute attention from fresh accepted evidence and must show unknown when semantic evidence is absent. Venus displays Eon state without scraping terminal content.

The first agent-workspace slice should compare no machine-readable surface with a deterministic local CLI or existing local socket for stable-ID list, tab and pane creation, directional or identity focus, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and view removal distinct from session termination. Bounded terminal observation remains a separate read-only capability owned through orb-p92. MCP may later adapt accepted Eon actions; it is not the first protocol, plugin system or authorization owner.

For eon-pxn, the chosen bounded Eon workspace composes multiple independent one-session Orbit endpoints as one product slice: Eon owns horizontal-tab and per-tab vertical-pane order, Venus materializes a visual accordion with one expanded pane and persistent collapsed headers, and direct workspace commands traverse tabs left or right and panes up or down without a picker. This does not authorize an Orbit multi-session process or give Orbit layout ownership.

Decide an Orbit process that hosts multiple sessions separately from Eon workspace topology, restart recovery separately from detach, remote terminal transport separately from web/mobile presentation, and remote environment orchestration separately from all three. Effects, search, semantic regions, observation and graphics remain separate candidates. Select exactly one frontier.

Accepted decision and update order:
1. Activate the minimum eon-pxn Eon owner for stable tab and pane identities, ordered topology, independent Orbit-session mappings, and only the semantic actions required by that topology.
2. Activate a separate Eon-owned managed interactive-environment child under eon-pxn. Eon owns its selected components, exact identities, private configuration, command projection, and product defaults; the tools retain native behavior and schema ownership.
3. Activate the Venus consumer for opaque horizontal tabs and the one-expanded vertical accordion. Orbit remains unchanged unless an exact owner-contract gap is found.
4. Prove the cross-repository dogfood workspace.
5. Only after the opaque workspace passes, separately activate the minimum Venus appearance capability for Eon-owned font, theme, bell, and default-background opacity policy.

The full managed-environment decision lives in eon-pxn. Orbit only launches the exact selected argv and retains process, PTY, terminal, and session authority; it does not own Nushell, prompt, editor, file-manager, Git UI, PATH, alias, theme, font, bell, or opacity policy. Opaque tabs do not wait for a general configuration system, plugin mechanism, observation plane, effects framework, remote support, or native Eon editor. A missing prerequisite pauses the frontier at its real owner rather than inviting a Venus or Orbit workaround.

title: Decide whether Venus and Orbit earn Eon graduation
description:
Decision gate: decide whether the proven Venus and Orbit pair earns the Eon implementation frontier after hardening, minimum native history, scrolling, selection and copy, and fresh Eon dogfood that includes one real coding-agent lifecycle. This Bead changes no runtime contract or implementation.

Required evidence:
- Exact accepted ORB-C and VEN-C proofs, revisions, compatibility order, platforms and every remaining P0 or P1 owner gap.
- The accepted workload envelope and the native-history end-to-end LOC, latency, CPU, memory, request, failure-state and compatibility evidence.
- Fresh native dogfood demonstrating whether client-independent process lifetime, coherent reattachment, one terminal authority and explicit failure ownership are materially valuable for ordinary terminal work and for one bounded real coding-agent task.
- A refreshed Canario comparison with separate distribution and mechanism evidence. Use `canarioterm/releases` commit `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d` and release `v2026.08.07.15`, built from private revision `canario@af91699`, for distribution evidence. Use Rio `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`, the final public Canario tree before extraction commit `e69b5fffef25abd5e649bf4ac205636551e54482`, for inspectable same-process lifetime and restoration mechanisms. Treat current private internals as unknown.
- Exact current Herdr evidence for durable agent terminals and client-independent work. Compare mechanisms and proved user contracts. Adoption, screenshots, commit counts and feature breadth carry no decision weight.

Protocol-gravity falsification:
Measure the full cost of ordinary history, scrolling, selection and copy across the boundary: owned code, protocol messages and bounds, repositories, handoffs, compatibility, failure states and runtime cost. Compare that tax with demonstrated process survival, independent client failure, replaceable clients and structured authority. Agent value receives credit only for the exact real workload completed in orb-bi4.6. Do not credit speculative observer, AgentRun, remote, multiplayer, web, plugin, provider integration or restart-persistence value.

Decision rule:
- Go only if dogfood makes the accepted lifetime and authority benefits materially useful, including the real agent task, and the cross-boundary cost remains proportionate and maintainable.
- No-go if an integrated shape satisfies the chosen contract more simply, Venus reconstructs Orbit truth, ordinary capabilities require disproportionate protocol ceremony, or agent benefit appears only in unimplemented future surfaces.
- A no-go records the smallest rollback or simplification boundary and implements nothing.
design:
Compare Venus and Orbit with the current Mars and Zellij path, Mars Next, Canario, zmx, justerm-core and Herdr. Separate Canario distribution evidence at `canarioterm/releases` `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d` and `v2026.08.07.15` from mechanism evidence in the final public Rio tree `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`. Inspect Herdr main `3a76fea2d858a7a5ef58615f1cc9aabaa30b80ee` and stable release `v0.8.0` for durable agent-terminal and transient-client contracts. Keep component references distinct from competing architectures.

Judge two demonstrated questions separately:
1. Is the one-authority structured terminal path coherent and worth its three-repository and protocol cost for ordinary terminal behavior?
2. Does a real coding-agent process materially benefit from surviving Venus loss and coherent reattachment without claiming any unimplemented agent-state, workspace, observer, control, remote or restore feature?

The real agent run is an ordinary PTY process. Graduation does not define AgentRun, provider status or an agent API. It determines whether the foundation improves the selected agent workflow enough to justify continuing toward the separately planned Eon agent-first workspace.

A go accepts Venus and Orbit as the Eon foundation and unblocks orb-bi4.7. It does not modify Nova, activate workspace or agent features, promote channels, add repositories, create compatibility windows or implement follow-up scope. A no-go records retained evidence and the user-selected retain or delete boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Summarize live presentation, lifecycle, native history, scrolling, selection, copy, accessibility, known limitations, actual Rust LOC, dependency footprint, maintenance risks, dogfood, performance, lost Zellij functionality and every P0 or P1 risk with exact proof revisions.
2. Audit the accepted performance envelope and explicit complete-frame decision rather than graduating from raw timings.
3. State whether Venus and Orbit are materially simpler and more coherent as the Eon foundation than the current Mars and Zellij chain, Mars Next or the closest applicable architecture.
4. State whether structured live presentation and host-owned history preserve rich capabilities without an unacceptable visible-screen or text-grid ceiling.
5. State whether scrolling, selection, copy, detach and reattach form a minimum useful terminal path rather than a protocol demonstration.
6. Record the exact real coding-agent CLI, bounded task and lifecycle evidence from orb-bi4.6. State whether Venus loss and reattachment materially improved that workflow and list every observed gap without converting it into an implemented or supported feature.
7. Credit agent value only from that evidence. Observer, AgentRun, machine-readable actions, provider semantics, remote execution, plugins and restart recovery remain speculative and receive zero graduation credit.
8. Measure the actual Orbit owner change, Venus consumer change, Eon pin update, compatibility sequence, commits, project-owned LOC and maintenance burden required by the accepted history baseline.
9. Compare the measured cost with demonstrated independent failure, replaceable-client, structured-state, forkability and real-agent lifecycle benefits.
10. Obtain and record one explicit user go or no-go with confidence.
11. On go, unblock orb-bi4.7 to select exactly one post-graduation frontier. On no-go, record the retain or delete choice and close orb-bi4.7 as not applicable.
12. Create no promotion, cleanup, UI, agent, remote, workspace, distribution or alternative-engine Bead without the corresponding user choice.
13. Audit immutable ORB-C and VEN-C proofs, protocol exceptions, governance checks, crate decisions, platform seams and changelogs.
14. Search, effects, semantic regions, agent observation, AgentRun, machine-readable actions, graphics, multiple sessions, workspace topology, restart recovery, remote transport, web, mobile and distribution remain unimplemented unless separately accepted.
notes:
Graduation decision

User decision: GO on 2026-08-08. Advisor confidence: 80 percent. Venus and Orbit earn graduation as the Eon foundation. This decision changes no product contract, proof revision, runtime, dependency, repository boundary, distribution channel or follow-up implementation.

Accepted proof set

- ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 are Proved at Orbit `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`; ORB-C10 is Proved at `292b2451c9a1d99390334771a681c7f481c996f2`. Orbit distribution revision `00b136318bea13e3f08d490468f069de6f6b9bd2` preserves them.
- Venus `2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832` consumes the exact ORBF v1 and ORBS v2 owner package. VEN-C1, VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4 and VEN-C7 are Proved at their indexed revisions. Venus materializes frames, captures native input, exposes accessibility and clipboard effects, and owns no PTY or terminal model.
- Eon manifest proof `c9e898c9ff889c2be4d4381a20676291bab65b49` pins Orbit `00b1363` and Venus `2d36c72`. EON-C1 proof `712c0834691c58b07e56494de25f98670b6a882e` and EON-C2 through EON-C4 composition proof `eae70e8d3ed4348b389f320dfd49d7db29478546` establish the accepted Nix-only Linux composition. EON-C5 through EON-C7 remain planned distribution work and carry no foundation correctness claim.
- The owner-first ORBS v2 change landed in Orbit, then Venus pinned the exact revision, then Eon pinned the accepted pair. No adapter, duplicate schema, feature probe, dual decoder or compatibility window exists.

Demonstrated value

Closed orb-bi4.6 consumed a fresh Eon run with Codex CLI 0.147.0 in a disposable Rust repository. Venus exited while Codex was active. Eon, Orbit, the PTY and Codex survived; `eon attach` opened a new Venus against the same session; the task completed; and independent format, test and Clippy checks passed. Provider semantic state remained unknown. The same component pair exercised 3,000 history rows, rapid wheel input, return to live, wrapped Unicode, wide-grapheme selection and copy, resize and reflow, Helix, Neovim, Yazi keyboard and application mouse, DEC 1007, output pressure, client loss and coherent reattachment.

The corrected sustained-output envelope passed at combined CPU p95 167 percent under the declared 200 percent ceiling, peak combined RSS 55.3 MiB and final convergence 13.6 ms. The native history proof completed 32 synchronous wheel round trips in 39.620976 ms with a 12,809-byte complete ORBS frame. The real-pair lifecycle proof observed coherent reattachment in 122 ms. These measurements retain their named workloads and do not become broad performance claims.

ORBF v1 carries styled graphemes, colors, cursor, title, working directory, hyperlinks, active-screen identity and explicit capability flags. Orbit owns retained history, viewport, selection and copy; Venus never reconstructs terminal state from text or PTY bytes. The accepted capability set preserves rich state without a visible-screen or text-grid ceiling. Kitty graphics remain declared unsupported.

Protocol and ownership cost

Orbit added 57 production and 370 test lines for authoritative viewport behavior. Selection and copy raised product Rust and tests from 6,454 to 7,161 lines, a further 707 lines. Current Orbit accounting is 7,183 product Rust lines, 765 governance Rust lines and two terminfo lines. The dependency-free `orbit-protocol` package owns 3,100 Rust lines, including 2,131 production and 969 test lines.

The accepted Venus history, selection, copy and accessibility slice changed 835 net Rust lines from its pre-slice baseline and added arboard 3.6.1 behind the native clipboard seam. Arboard required 15 Venus production lines and 12 all-target lock packages. Current Venus accounting is 4,359 Rust source lines, 363 integration-test lines and 5,301 tracked handwritten lines. Eon keeps one component manifest and launch owner; its current scorecard includes 1,026 Rust source and test lines.

At the exact comparison revisions, Eon, Orbit and Venus contain about 12,931 tracked Rust lines across their scorecards. Nova `cf313431ca0b08352b0a5b4b0beb2341aee5568a`, Mars `2b63717135a72ef330d8c2da8ca4cde59c22d739` and Yazelix Zellij `bbccdea6eda81f314151160f9b3f8882a26478ec` contain about 521,170 tracked Rust lines. These raw maintenance surfaces do not equate feature sets, but the gap supports the smaller ownership conclusion. Nova remains an independent product because Eon still excludes its layouts, plugins and multi-session workspace behavior.

Comparator result

Canario publishes builds through `canarioterm/releases` commit `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d`; release `v2026.08.07.15` records private source `canario@af91699`. Current private internals remain unknown. Rio `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`, the final public tree before extraction `e69b5fffef25abd5e649bf4ac205636551e54482`, remains the inspectable integrated comparator. It keeps PTYs in the application, restarts shells and restores layout, CWD, title and text scrollback. That shape has lower protocol cost but fails the selected live-process survival contract.

Herdr main `3a76fea2d858a7a5ef58615f1cc9aabaa30b80ee` and stable release `v0.8.0` publish a server/client contract for durable agent terminals and transient clients. Herdr also owns workspaces, multiple panes, restart restoration, remote attachment, agent heuristics, integrations, plugins and an agent API. Graduation accepts its process-continuity lesson and gives zero credit to those broader surfaces.

The Canario integrated shape cannot satisfy ORB-C1, and Herdr corroborates the value of a separate durable terminal owner. Neither reference justifies compatibility or adoption. Complete frames remain accepted because the measured envelope passed; patches, dirty-row extraction and a second renderer remain deferred.

Risks and limits

The audit found one approved protocol exception: orb-bi4.2 comment 14 records the user's 2026-08-04 one-time authorization to reconstruct baseline, reference and crate-gate evidence after those timing rules were adopted during the candidate. The exception applies only to orb-bi4.2, does not claim the records predated implementation, and does not extend to another Bead. Later accepted proofs reran the canonical checks.

No known P0 or P1 correctness blocker remains. Open or deferred P1 items are decision or feature scope: orb-bi4.7, agent observation, ordered effects, Venus hyperlinks and Eon workspace planning. Linux/Nix and Xwayland carry the accepted proof. macOS, native Wayland quality, candidate-list IME quality, proprietary NVIDIA packaging, direct distribution and restart persistence remain unproved. One synthetic wheel delta of 80 disconnected Venus, while representative rapid unit input passed and reattachment recovered. Optional emoji and Yazi icons showed fallback boxes. Search, effects, graphics, richer selection, multiple sessions, layouts, remote transport, web and mobile remain separate decisions.

The selected dependency cost remains material: libghostty-vt 0.2.1 builds pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` through Zig, the source checkout measured about 155 MiB, Venus carries a native GPU, shaping and accessibility stack, and the Eon Nix closure is about 1.46 GiB. Exact lockstep across three repositories remains a maintenance cost. Dogfood, bounded failure ownership and the smaller maintenance surface justify that cost at this stage.

Two nonblocking metadata discrepancies remain outside this authorized planning-only run: the Orbit crate index retains an obsolete sentence that Venus still consumes ORBS v1 until `ven-4sn`, and Venus VEN-C3/VEN-C4 rows retain historical partial-ORB-C7 wording against their original consumed proof despite the current Eon pair pinning proved ORB-C7. The canonical current consumer relationship in Orbit and Eon contract indexes is correct.

Decision consequence

Graduation unblocks orb-bi4.7 to choose exactly one post-graduation frontier. This run creates no implementation bead, starts no frontier, changes no changelog and does not promote a distribution channel. Nova remains unchanged.
close_reason: GO at 80 percent confidence: accepted Orbit, Venus, and Eon proofs plus real Codex dogfood demonstrate useful process survival and coherent terminal authority at proportionate measured cost; orb-bi4.7 may select one frontier.

title: Extract the canonical ORBF v1 codec for Venus
description: Create the smallest Orbit-owned, platform-neutral Rust protocol surface that lets Orbit and Venus consume one canonical ORBF v1 interpretation at exact revisions without changing the accepted wire contract.

It owns ORBF v1 version and bounds, canonical frame data, bounded decode and validation, byte encoding, and complete-frame revision reduction. The existing Orbit server consumes the package while libghostty extraction remains in Orbit; Venus later consumes the exact same package from a pinned Orbit Git revision. Preserve ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 behavior and byte compatibility. Do not add a new wire version, public trace format, fourth repository, crates.io publication, renderer, raw PTY path, terminal state, schema generator, or external dependency.

1. An Execution baseline records current HEAD, policy hash, Bead revision, ORB-C4/ORB-C6/ORB-C7 routing, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and session identity.

8. No external crate, generated mirror, adapter, compatibility window, trace format, command, or additional binary is added.
9. Canonical Rust checks and governance pass; owned LOC, package/dependency footprint, byte compatibility, portability disposition, and remaining gaps are recorded.
10. Touched proved contracts remain partial until an accepted proof-bearing commit, then ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 advance to that exact revision; ORB-C7 remains honestly partial unless its full hardening gap is closed.
notes: User approval on 2026-08-04 explicitly selected the Orbit-owned protocol package and a narrowly scoped implementation Bead after ven-upt.1 reported the missing canonical consumer surface. This Bead preserves existing product contracts; it does not activate Venus graphical implementation.

comments.text:
Crate gate — accepted dependency and package decision — 2026-08-04

Decision already authorized by the user after the protocol-boundary stop: add one internal, dependency-free, platform-neutral orbit-protocol workspace library and make yazelix-orbit depend on it by path. Do not add an external crate, publish target, schema generator, compatibility window, fourth repository, or second decoder. This gate records the comparison behind that accepted choice; it does not expand the approval.

Affected contracts: ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7; Venus will consume the exact accepted Orbit Git revision for VEN-C1 through VEN-C4. Existing product dependencies remain libc 0.2.189 and libghostty-vt 0.2.1 in the root binary only.

Candidate matrix:

1. Selected — internal std-only orbit-protocol package with the existing explicit little-endian ORBF v1 codec.
Fit/ownership: exact fit; one format owner, reusable by Orbit and Venus, no PTY/terminal dependency leakage, no wire revision. Estimated code movement is the existing roughly 60-line encoder plus roughly 100-line test decoder, with owned public values, errors, reducer, and focused tests added in the same package; no duplicated schema. Cost: one direct workspace path edge, zero external direct/transitive/native/build/Nix dependencies, no proc macros, no generated files. API/versioning: private Git-pinned package, publish=false, explicit VERSION=1 and strict errors; Orbit controls upgrades with its proof commit. License/security: project-owned; checked arithmetic and pre-allocation bounds can match the exact hostile-input contract. Platform: std-only byte/value logic is neutral across Linux, macOS, and a future wasm32 consumer. Accessibility/input/browser: no policy or OS API is embedded, so those remain consumer concerns.

2. Root library target with terminal features, no new package.
Fit/ownership: can expose a decoder but couples consumer resolution to the yazelix-orbit package and its libc/libghostty build graph unless terminal dependencies become optional features. That feature split adds manifest states and makes it easier for protocol and terminal ownership to drift within one crate. Project LOC is superficially smaller but consumer/build isolation is worse. Rejected because the acceptance criterion requires a consumer build that cannot compile PTY, libc, libghostty, or governance code.

3. Keep the encoder private and hand Venus a separate decoder.
Fit/ownership: zero dependency cost but creates the forbidden second schema and makes byte drift invisible until cross-repository integration. Rejected by the Orbit/Venus ownership contract.

4. bincode 2.0.1, MIT (the crates.io latest, 3.0.0, is a deliberately nonfunctional compile_error placeholder and is not a credible candidate).
Fit: mature general Rust binary codec, but its derived representation is not accepted ORBF v1; preserving v1 would still need the owned parser/encoder. Default 2.0.1 adds bincode_derive and unty, with proc-macro/build graph; serde is another optional edge. Owned LOC is not removed for the existing format. Pure Rust and broadly portable, but upgrades/configuration become wire decisions. Rejected: dependency cost and format instability for zero contract gain.

5. postcard 1.1.3, MIT OR Apache-2.0.
Fit: compact/no_std serde format, but it changes bytes and needs serde plus cobs and default heapless support; preserving ORBF again leaves a custom adapter. Pure Rust, macOS/wasm credible, no native dependency, but its embedded-oriented framing and serde data model do not prove the terminal-specific bounds or exact accepted revision. Rejected: more transitive and upgrade surface without removing the canonical codec.

6. prost 0.14.4 / Protocol Buffers, Apache-2.0.
Fit: mature schema evolution and multi-language ecosystem, but ORBF v1 is not protobuf. It adds bytes and prost-derive at runtime and normally prost-build plus a .proto/generated source workflow at build time; that increases build, cache, Nix, and upgrade surfaces and creates generated artifacts. Browser interoperability is strong in a different protocol, but no remote or general multi-language protocol is authorized. Rejected: wire change, generator, schema compatibility surface, and materially greater cost.

7. rkyv 0.8.17, MIT.
Fit: high-performance archive/zero-copy model, but archived Rust layout, alignment/pointer-width choices, validation, and its broad dependency set are unnecessary for a small bounded network frame and make cross-target stability a larger concern. Defaults include bytecheck plus derive and supporting crates such as hashbrown, munge, ptr_meta, rancor, and rend. No native build is required, but compile/upgrade/security review cost is highest of the pure-Rust candidates. Rejected: no measured zero-copy pressure, wrong stability shape, changes bytes.

8. capnp 0.27.0 / Cap’n Proto, MIT.
Fit: explicit schema and cross-language evolution, but requires a new wire and generated bindings; normal development adds capnpc/schema compilation and may require the external capnp tool, creating build and Nix/platform cost. It is credible for a future separately approved multi-language/remote protocol, not for exact v1 extraction. Rejected.

9. Separate protocol repository/package publication.
Fit: strongest physical isolation but adds a fourth version/release/coordination surface and conflicts with the accepted exact-Git-revision consumption model. Rejected by the user-approved scope.

Focused proof and disputed claims: cargo info and normalized crates.io manifests were inspected for bincode 2.0.1/3.0.0, postcard 1.1.3, prost 0.14.4, rkyv 0.8.17, and capnp 0.27.0. bincode 3.0.0 contains compile_error!("https://xkcd.com/2347/"). The accepted e4fde443 Orbit source proves the existing format already has a compact encoder and test decoder, so an external serializer removes no required v1 logic.

Consequences of the accepted choice: Cargo.toml adds crates/protocol as a workspace member and orbit-protocol as a root path dependency; crates/protocol/Cargo.toml declares edition 2024 and publish=false with no dependencies. Cargo.lock should only gain the local package edge. docs/CRATES.md will record this durable decision. Root production maps libghostty state into protocol-owned values; the protocol crate never imports libghostty, libc, sockets, renderer APIs, platform APIs, or governance. The first check is an exact accepted rich-frame decode/re-encode plus bounded hostile-input and strict revision tests, followed by cargo tree/metadata evidence that orbit-protocol has no external dependency graph.

title: Evaluate a Bend2 proof model of Orbit attachment semantics
description:
## Contract routing

This is a bounded research and decision spike for an external proof model. It changes no ORB product contract and does not authorize a Bend2 runtime dependency, production rewrite, generated C/CUDA integration, permanent proof directory, hosted CI job, protocol/schema copy, or change of implementation language. The Rust Orbit implementation and indexed contract proofs remain authoritative.

The first experiment models only the cohesive ORB-C1/ORB-C4/ORB-C7 attachment-and-revision cluster. Selection, terminal semantics, wire encoding, PTY syscalls, graphics, persistence, and Venus are excluded. A successful result may justify a separate user-approved adoption or expansion Bead; it does not widen itself.

Impact: potentially medium if Bend2 expresses a small readable machine-checked lifecycle invariant. Effort: M. Risk: high because Bend2 is unreleased and an external model has an unavoidable refinement gap from Rust. Confidence: medium that the spike can reach a useful adopt/reject decision, low that it should become production infrastructure.

## Current state and evidence

As of 2026-08-11, the public `VictorTaelin/Bend2` repository reports `Bend2 - WIP`, has no commits or license, and cannot supply an inspectable proof language. Do not begin from announcements, private demonstrations, Bend1, or inferred syntax. Begin only from a public exact Bend2 release or commit with source, license, proof semantics, documentation, and a reproducible toolchain.

Orbit evidence:

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` defines ORB-C1 client-independent PTY lifetime, ORB-C4 complete-frame attachment plus strictly ordered revisions, and ORB-C7 bounded slow/broken-client behavior.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:338-367` owns strict complete-frame revision reduction.
- `crates/protocol/src/session.rs:562-598` owns bounded role-specific attachment framing before payload buffering.
- `src/main.rs:236+` keeps the authoritative revision in the single owner loop.
- `src/main.rs:1061-1075` owns checked revision advance and detach-side selection cleanup.
- `tests/lifecycle.rs` and `src/presentation.rs` provide the executable real-PTY traces that any abstract model must map to without replacing.

## Prerequisites

- Blocked by `orb-ll1.1`; model the exact accepted post-ORBS-v3 revision, not the active dirty candidate.
- Bend2 must have an inspectable public source revision or release, an explicit license compatible with this research use, official language/proof documentation, a reproducible Linux toolchain, and a way to verify proofs non-interactively.
- Do not start while another issue or agent changes the selected Orbit state-transition surface.

The Kani and Verus evaluation Beads are comparison evidence only and are not sequencing dependencies.

## Required references before model code

Required: current `AGENTS.md`; exact accepted ORB-C1, ORB-C4, and ORB-C7 proofs; the complete accepted owner-loop attachment/detach/frame/pressure paths and their real-PTY tests; `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/RATIONALE.md`; exact public Bend2 source, license, compiler/runtime, proof checker, trust model, totality/consistency claims, numeric and linear/resource semantics, FFI/extraction behavior, supported platforms, and official examples at one immutable identity.

Comparison only: the sibling Kani and Verus spikes, Lean/Agda-style external models, and Bend1/HVM history. Rejected: treating creator claims as proof semantics, importing Bend1 behavior, or copying Orbit Rust into a second executable implementation.

If repository production code, tests, manifests, docs, generated files, or configuration would be edited, first claim this non-epic Bead, record the execution baseline, and pass the evidence-first gate. Any tool/dependency or manifest change requires the full crate/dependency gate and user approval. Hosted automation requires a separately justified CI contract.

## Smallest model

Define a finite, explicit transition system independent of terminal cell contents:

- State: PTY/session liveness, zero-or-one attached client, authoritative revision, whether the attachment's initial complete frame has been emitted, and bounded client-output disposition.
- Events: attach attempt, complete initial frame, authoritative frame publication, client detach/failure, output pressure, PTY close, and shutdown.
- Observations: attachment outcome, complete-frame revision, disconnect/failure, and PTY/session liveness.

Prove only:

1. At most one client owns attachment in every reachable state.
2. Client detach/failure never changes a live PTY/session to dead.
3. A successful attachment cannot expose a later revision before its coherent initial complete frame.
4. Every later exposed frame revision is strictly greater than the previously exposed revision.
5. Bounded client-output pressure disconnects/fails that client without creating a second attachment or unbounded modeled history.

Use the smallest numeric domain sufficient to expose ordering mistakes, then state exactly whether Bend2 proves the invariant generically or only for the finite bound. Include one intentionally invalid transition or inverted theorem and demonstrate that Bend2 rejects it.

Do not model ORBF/ORBS bytes, terminal cells, libghostty, PTY/syscall behavior, selection, effects, viewport, search, graphics, persistence, multiple sessions, multiple clients, remote transport, Eon/Venus policy, or performance.

## Method and decision

1. Pin the exact accepted Orbit subject and exact Bend2 identity.
2. Record Bend2's trusted computing base, proof-checking semantics, consistency/termination boundaries, axioms/unsafe escapes, numeric semantics, and whether executable evaluation can diverge from proofs.
3. Build the model in a temporary isolated location with no Orbit manifest or source changes. Record its complete hash, owned LOC, command, duration, memory, assumptions, and proof output.
4. Map each modeled state/event/observation to exact Rust symbols and real-PTY tests. Name every behavior abstracted away; do not claim refinement between Bend2 and Rust.
5. Mutate one transition or theorem so the checker fails for the expected reason.
6. Compare proof clarity, coverage, maintenance, agent readability, toolchain/CI cost, and refinement gap with no external model and any completed Kani/Verus evidence.
7. Close with adopt, defer, or reject. Adoption means only that a separate user-approved Bead may persist or automate the model.

## Acceptance

1. A public Bend2 release/commit, license, source, proof semantics, toolchain, trust boundary, and exact non-interactive verification command are recorded. If any is unavailable, the Bead remains deferred or closes rejected without model code.
2. The model contains only the declared attachment/revision state machine and all five invariants; owned model/proof LOC and duplicated concepts are counted.
3. Every modeled element maps to exact accepted Orbit Rust and contract evidence, while every abstraction and the Rust-to-model refinement gap is explicit.
4. The positive proof succeeds and one deliberate negative mutation fails for the intended reason at the exact pinned Bend2 revision.
5. Proof bounds, axioms, unsafe/trusted declarations, numeric assumptions, excluded events, command, duration, memory, model hash, and raw-result location are recorded.
6. No Bend2 code enters Orbit production, no generated artifact executes in Eon, no product schema or contract changes, and no ORB proof revision/status is updated.
7. Closure records adopt/defer/reject, comparison with no model and available Kani/Verus evidence, retained-value proposal if any, removal cost, and the required fresh user decision before persistence or CI.

## Verification

Against the unchanged accepted Orbit revision:

- `cargo fmt --check` exits 0.
- `cargo check --locked` exits 0.
- `cargo test --locked` exits 0.
- `cargo test --locked -p orbit-protocol` exits 0.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .` exits 0.
- `git diff --check` exits 0.
- The exact release-supported Bend2 non-interactive proof command is recorded and proves the declared positive model while rejecting the deliberate negative mutation.
- `br sync --flush-only` persists only the research record.

## Stop conditions

Stop if Bend2 remains unpublished, lacks an explicit usable license or proof documentation, cannot verify non-interactively, requires a protocol mirror or production redesign, cannot express the transition system without trusted axioms that erase the invariants, or progress requires a repository, dependency, CI, compatibility, contract, or cross-repository change without fresh user approval.

title: Evaluate Kani for canonical Orbit protocol proofs
description:
## Contract routing

This is a bounded research and decision spike. It changes no ORB product contract and does not authorize a runtime dependency, permanent proof harness, hosted CI job, protocol/schema copy, or production refactor. Candidate evidence may assess whether Kani can harden the existing proofs for ORB-C3, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C7, and ORB-C9, but it cannot change their indexed status or proof revision.

Impact: medium-high if Kani proves a security- or correctness-relevant property against canonical Rust. Effort: S-M. Risk: medium. Confidence: high that the experiment can reach a clear adopt/reject result.

## Why and evidence

- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:320-335` owns checked ORBF size accounting and the 4 MiB bound.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:338-367` owns complete-frame reduction and strict revision monotonicity.
- `crates/protocol/src/session.rs:562-598` validates ORBS magic, revision, flags, role-specific payload bounds, and minimum lengths before payload-sized buffering.
- `crates/protocol/src/session.rs:980-1007` owns bounded framing and exact-message rejection.
- `src/main.rs:1061-1065` fails explicitly when the authoritative presentation revision is exhausted.
- `docs/CRATES.md` records `orbit-protocol` as a private, dependency-free, platform-neutral owner with extensive finite tests; `orb-fuzz-orbit-codecs-kf5` separately plans fuzzing but does not provide exhaustive bounded proof.

The decision is whether Kani adds material confidence against the production Rust owner without duplicating its schema, weakening assumptions until the claim is empty, or imposing more toolchain/maintenance cost than the proved property is worth.

## Prerequisite

Blocked by `orb-ll1.1`. Evaluate the accepted post-ORBS-v3 protocol revision, not its active dirty candidate. Do not start while another issue or agent changes `crates/protocol` or the selected proof surface.

## Required references before proof code

Required: current `AGENTS.md`; exact accepted ORB contracts and proof revisions; current `orbit-protocol` production code, tests, callers, `docs/CRATES.md`, and `docs/REFERENCES.md`; `orb-audit-orbit-protocols-bkk`; `orb-fuzz-orbit-codecs-kf5`; and Kani's official documentation and source at one exact release or commit, including supported Rust features, proof harness semantics, contracts, loop/unwind bounds, assumptions, soundness limits, license, and toolchain requirements.

Comparison only: current finite Rust tests and the planned fuzzing shape. Rejected scope: a handwritten Kani protocol model, alternate decoder, copied constants, or proof over a stub that removes the property under test.

If repository production code, tests, manifests, or generated files would be edited, first claim this non-epic Bead, record the required execution baseline, and pass the evidence-first gate. A direct/tool dependency or manifest change requires the full crate gate and user approval. Hosted automation requires a separately justified CI contract.

## Smallest experiment

1. Record the exact accepted subject revision and compare three shapes: current tests plus no new verifier; the accepted fuzzing plan; and exact Kani.
2. Select one smallest non-trivial property that exercises canonical production Rust. Preferred order:
   - every syntactically complete ORBS header either rejects before payload buffering or yields a length within the role-specific maximum;
   - checked ORBF/session size arithmetic cannot overflow into acceptance;
   - `FrameReducer` never replaces its current frame with an equal or older revision;
   - a bounded canonical encode/decode property if Kani can construct valid production values without a parallel schema.
3. Keep initial harness code outside production ownership and avoid manifest changes. Record every assumption, stub, unwind/loop bound, explored input domain, proof time, peak memory, and whether the property is bounded or unbounded.
4. Run one negative mutation or assertion inversion to demonstrate that the harness can fail for the intended reason.
5. End with adopt, defer, or reject. Adoption means only that a separate user-approved implementation Bead may be proposed; it does not retain candidate code automatically.

## Acceptance

1. The record pins exact Kani source/release, license, Rust/toolchain requirements, Nix/offline feasibility, supported target shape, and replacement/removal cost.
2. The candidate matrix compares no new verifier, fuzzing, and Kani on proof strength, false-confidence risk, owned proof LOC, build/CI time, maintenance, portability, and agent readability.
3. At least one meaningful property runs against canonical production Rust, or the exact language/library/tool limitation is reproduced and justifies rejection.
4. The proof record states its full input domain, assumptions, stubs, bounds, exclusions, command, duration, and counterexample behavior. A bounded result is never described as universal.
5. No second ORBF/ORBS schema, decoder, constants inventory, product behavior, compatibility surface, or runtime dependency is created.
6. Existing canonical tests remain the executable behavior oracle. The result cannot mark an ORB contract Proved, refresh its proof commit, or displace real-PTY/native evidence.
7. Closure notes record adopt/defer/reject, the smallest valuable retained shape if any, rejected alternatives, exact commands/results, and a user decision gate before durable adoption.

## Verification

Against the unchanged accepted repository revision:

- `cargo fmt --check` exits 0.
- `cargo check --locked` exits 0.
- `cargo test --locked` exits 0.
- `cargo test --locked -p orbit-protocol` exits 0.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .` exits 0.
- `git diff --check` exits 0.
- The exact release-supported `cargo kani --harness <selected-harness>` command is recorded and either proves the declared property or produces the captured rejection evidence.
- `br sync --flush-only` persists only the research record.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the accepted subject changes, an active agent owns the surface, Kani requires a protocol mirror or production redesign, assumptions erase the relevant invalid-input space, the verifier cannot consume the canonical Rust subset, or progress requires a manifest, CI, compatibility, contract, or cross-repository change without fresh user approval.

title: Evaluate Verus for canonical Orbit reducer proofs
description:
## Contract routing

This is a bounded research and decision spike. It changes no ORB product contract and does not authorize a runtime dependency, permanent proof module, hosted CI job, protocol/schema copy, or production rewrite into Verus syntax. Candidate evidence may assess whether Verus can harden the existing proof architecture for ORB-C3, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C7, and ORB-C9, but it cannot change their indexed status or proof revision.

Impact: medium if a concise specification stays mechanically attached to canonical Rust. Effort: M. Risk: medium-high because Verus supports a deliberate Rust subset and may require proof-oriented code shape. Confidence: medium.

## Why and evidence

- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:338-367` is a small deterministic reducer whose invariant is that accepted complete frames strictly advance revision while rejection preserves the current frame.

- `crates/protocol/src/session.rs:562-598` separates header admission from payload decoding and owns pre-allocation bounds.
