title: Fuzz the accepted Orbit wire codecs
description:
Repository-hardening task with no new user-visible behavior or product contract. After orb-j0m.3 closes at an accepted ORBS v2 proof, run one bounded manual fuzzing campaign against the canonical orbit-protocol ORBS and ORBF decoders.

The goal is to exercise the exact production decoders with arbitrary bounded bytes and prove that malformed input is rejected without a panic, hang, sanitizer finding, decoder-controlled unbounded allocation, or invalid accepted value. Any discovered input is minimized and becomes a deterministic regression check before its owner is fixed.

Contract routing:
- Changes no ORB-C contract, wire bytes, bounds, runtime policy, compatibility promise, supported platform, or proof status by itself.
- Hardens the accepted decoder implementations supporting ORB-C3, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, and ORB-C7. Reconfirm exact IDs and proof revisions at activation.
- Owns only Orbit protocol test tooling and evidence. A production defect or intentional protocol change stops for separate product scope.

Out of scope:
- Fuzzing libghostty or its VT parser, the full Orbit server, PTY or socket lifecycle, Venus, Eon, continuous fuzzing infrastructure, per-push or scheduled CI, a runtime dependency, a general property-testing framework, remote input, a new protocol revision, or a general security proof.
design:
Implementation plan:

1. Start only after orb-j0m.3 closes with an accepted ORBS v2 proof. Record an Execution baseline for this one test-tooling issue before any tracked fuzz manifest, target, seed, script, workflow, Nix, or documentation edit.
2. Pass a Reference and tool gate before edits. Required primary evidence: the exact cargo-fuzz release and Rust Fuzz Book; the exact Rust nightly, LLVM, libFuzzer, and sanitizer behavior it invokes; the accepted orbit-protocol source and deterministic codec corpus; and current Ghostty AFL++ work only as comparison evidence for upstream VT ownership. Compare cargo-fuzz, direct libFuzzer wiring, a larger deterministic corpus, and no fuzzing. Preserve the user-selected cargo-fuzz shape if it remains maintained and suitable.
3. Call the public production ORBS and ORBF decoders directly. Reuse the accepted canonical corpus as seeds and add no handwritten schema, alternate decoder, public trace format, adapter, runtime mode, or product binary.
4. Use the fewest targets that still give each independent decoder useful coverage. Bound input length, total time or executions, memory, artifact paths, and timeout behavior. Record the exact command, random seed where supported, starting-corpus identity, toolchain, sanitizer set, duration, executions, coverage counters, peak memory, crashes, timeouts, and out-of-memory results.
5. Treat panic, abort, sanitizer finding, hang, timeout on bounded work, decoder-controlled excessive allocation, or acceptance of an invalid typed value as a failure. Rejection of arbitrary bytes is normal.
6. Minimize every finding. Add the smallest deterministic regression to the normal suite before any correction. If the root cause is product code, protocol behavior, or an accepted bound, leave this Bead open and stop for one separately authorized owner fix rather than changing the protocol inside fuzz tooling.
7. Keep the campaign manual. Run the first baseline after ORBS v2 acceptance, then rerun after codec or bound changes and before a release that carries those changes. Do not add hosted continuous fuzzing, per-push or scheduled CI, or a default full-workspace fuzz job.
8. Keep generated corpora, logs, and crash artifacts untracked. Track only the minimum target, stable high-value seeds if they materially improve coverage, and deterministic regressions. Any test-only Cargo surface must remain isolated from the normal product and workspace dependency graph.

Portability disposition: neutral protocol hardening performed on one recorded supported host. It proves no PTY, renderer, libghostty, macOS runtime, or full-product behavior.

No CHANGELOG entry is expected. Update README LOC accounting only if tracked handwritten fuzz or regression files change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-j0m.3 is closed at an accepted proof-bearing revision and the baseline records exact ORBS and ORBF versions, affected ORB-C3 through ORB-C5 and ORB-C7 implementations as hardened rather than changed, and permitted tracked surfaces.
2. The pre-edit Reference and tool gate records exact cargo-fuzz, Rust nightly, LLVM/libFuzzer, sanitizer, orbit-protocol, and comparison-only Ghostty identities, licenses, maintenance state, alternatives, selected shape, and exit condition.
3. The targets invoke the canonical production ORBS and ORBF decoders with arbitrary bounded byte slices. They do not mirror the schema, parse VT, launch Orbit, or create another protocol owner.
4. The accepted seed corpus includes representative valid and invalid ORBS and ORBF values from deterministic checks. Rejection is accepted; every successful decode satisfies the existing canonical typed invariants without a second implementation of those invariants.
5. One bounded campaign records exact commands, host, toolchains, sanitizer set, maximum input, time or execution budget, corpus identity, coverage observations, peak memory, and counts for crashes, sanitizer reports, hangs, timeouts, and out-of-memory failures.
6. There are zero unexplained panics, aborts, sanitizer findings, hangs, decoder-controlled excessive allocations, or invalid accepted values. A nonzero result blocks closure.
7. Every finding is minimized and preserved as one deterministic normal-suite regression before correction. A product or contract correction is separately scoped and owned; this Bead does not hide, suppress, or absorb it.
8. Generated corpus and artifacts remain untracked. Any tracked fuzz target, manifest, stable seed, or helper is the minimum reproducible surface, adds no runtime dependency or product behavior, and stays outside the default product build and normal workspace graph.
9. The resulting manual trigger is recorded as after codec or bound changes and before a release carrying those changes. No continuous service, per-push job, schedule, CI matrix, general fuzz framework, or full-suite fuzz run is added.
10. Canonical locked Rust, governance, and git diff checks required by tracked changes pass. No ORB-C proof advances solely from fuzz output.
11. Closure records exact revision, identities, command, budgets, corpus and artifact disposition, results, regressions, dependency and LOC impact, portability, limitations, and whether the accepted codecs are clean enough for their next consumer.
notes:
User decision on 2026-08-07: adopt a low-priority bounded cargo-fuzz campaign for the accepted ORBS and ORBF decoders and rerun it after wire-codec changes or before relevant releases.

This decision supersedes the earlier orb-bi4.5 conditional deferral only for this explicit bounded protocol campaign. It does not authorize libghostty fuzzing, full-server fuzzing, continuous infrastructure, remote exposure, a general property framework, or an open-ended security program.

Why this owns a separate Bead: orbit-protocol is the Eon-owned trust boundary and ORBS v2 changes it. Ghostty now fuzzes its own VT parser and stream processor upstream, but that evidence cannot cover Orbit session framing, frame decoding, declared bounds, or typed acceptance.

Expected implementation risk is LOW to MEDIUM. The main risk is test-tool and nightly churn, not product architecture. Stop if useful coverage would require a mirrored schema, product-only hooks, a protocol change, or a persistent hosted service.

title: Prove host-owned history, native scrolling, selection, and copy
description:
Planning container for the minimum useful native-terminal history baseline before Eon dogfood and graduation.

Ownership:
- Orbit and its sole libghostty terminal own retained history, the authoritative viewport, active selection, and copied text.
- Venus owns native gesture capture, display and accessibility from the current complete ORBF frame, explicit copy action, and the native clipboard side effect.
- Venus has no history page cache, stable row tokens, row-anchor table, snapshot mirror, or second terminal/history model.

Contract routing:
- orb-j0m.2 is complete. ORB-C8 is proved at 840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0 and preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7.
- orb-j0m.3 is complete. ORB-C9 is proved at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 and preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C8.
- ORB-C9 deliberately replaces ORBS v1 with ORBS v2. The accepted owner-first breaking order is Orbit proof, Venus ven-4sn consumer update, then orb-j0m.4 acceptance; there is no adapter, dual support, feature probe, or compatibility window.
- orb-j0m.5 changes no product contract and runs one direct Valgrind Memcheck lifecycle against the exact accepted selection-capable Orbit revision.
- orb-j0m.4 is the no-code cross-repository acceptance gate after the Orbit owner, Valgrind hardening, and Venus consumer proofs.
- Complete ordered ORBF frames remain the only structured presentation and resynchronization authority. Search remains separate in orb-qcc.

This epic is a planning container. It must not be claimed for production code, tests, manifests, protocol edits, or contract-index edits.
design:
Run after the closed orb-bi4.5 visible-state hardening gate.

Execute one frontier at a time:
1. orb-j0m.1 records the accepted direct libghostty-native boundary and closes the discarded stable-history-identity decision.
2. orb-j0m.2 is complete: Orbit routes existing ORBS v1 wheel and key input from authoritative modes, drives the libghostty viewport, and publishes complete frames under ORB-C8.
3. orb-j0m.3 is complete: ORB-C9 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 adds bounded current-viewport cell selection and authoritative frozen plain-text copy through ORBS v2. It uses fresh libghostty selection snapshots resolved from the current viewport, not a page cache, durable row identity, or the more capable tracked selection-gesture state machine.
4. orb-j0m.5 runs one deterministic selection-capable Orbit lifecycle directly under Valgrind Memcheck. It is manual Linux hardening, changes no product contract, and does not enter default per-push CI.
5. Venus ven-4sn is re-primed against the accepted Orbit shape, then consumes exact Orbit revisions and implements native gesture capture, display, accessibility, failure, and clipboard policy without a page cache.
6. orb-j0m.4 performs no-code acceptance against the real Orbit and Venus pair after orb-j0m.5.

Reuse the accepted owner loop and libghostty-vt 0.2.1. The required surfaces already exist: Terminal.scroll_viewport, authoritative mouse state, current-viewport GridRef resolution, Selection snapshots, Terminal.set_selection, bounded Terminal.format_selection_buf, and render-state selected-cell projection.

ORB-C8 is the viewport source of truth: client loss preserves the current Orbit-owned viewport and reattachment starts from that view. Loss or detach clears only transient selection interaction and copy state. The stale orb-j0m.1 return-to-bottom sentence is superseded by the accepted ORB-C8 proof.

The accepted orb-j0m.3 change is an owner-first breaking replacement of ORBS v1 with ORBS v2 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757. Venus ven-4sn owns the exact consumer-pin update from c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6; no adapter, compatibility window, dual support, or feature probe is authorized.

The current cell-only slice deliberately does not instantiate selection::Gesture. If the user later chooses rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, word or line selection, multiclick behavior, deep press, or output selection, the new slice must inspect and reuse the exact then-current public libghostty selection::Gesture and related selection helpers as the terminal-semantic owner. Venus captures native pointer events; Orbit resolves terminal-bound gesture semantics and Selection snapshots unless a separately approved contract changes that boundary. Stop before implementing local click-count, word-boundary, line-boundary, autoscroll, or tracked-anchor semantics when the public API is absent or insufficient.

The simple local round-trip and complete-frame path remains the baseline. Coalescing, paging, patches, caching, richer selection, or a new dependency require measured need and a later user choice. orb-qcc and orb-3gf remain outside this batch and must be re-primed before activation because the native baseline promises no durable row identity.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-j0m.1 remains the closed user-approved native-boundary decision; later accepted contracts supersede any conflicting proposed behavior in that decision record.
2. orb-j0m.2 remains closed with ORB-C8 proved at 840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0: Orbit owns mouse routing and viewport state, byte-producing key input returns a scrolled primary viewport to live, disconnect preserves the viewport, and reattachment projects the current view.

5. orb-j0m.3 proves bounded current-viewport cell selection and exact frozen copy across wrapping, hard breaks, Unicode, combining and wide graphemes, reverse drag, stale frame rejection, mutation cancellation, resize and reflow, screen transitions, client loss, oversized text, and pressure while preserving ORB-C1 through ORB-C8.
6. orb-j0m.5 runs one deterministic real Orbit lifecycle directly under Valgrind Memcheck against the exact accepted selection-capable revision before cross-repository acceptance. It fails memory errors, definite or indirect leaks, and descriptor misuse or leaks; reports and classifies possibly lost memory without initially failing; and adds no Cargo wrapper, full-suite run, per-push CI, product mode, or product contract.

10. New coordinates, revisions, formatted text, work, and queued bytes reuse or define explicit numeric bounds with deterministic rejection or clamping before expensive work.
11. orb-upstream-libghostty-reference-loss-dck remains deferred and independent. No upstream change, fork, private adapter, paging plane, snapshot, or new dependency is required.

Any later richer-selection bead treats exact then-current public libghostty selection::Gesture and related word, line, output, drag, and autoscroll helpers as required-before-code evidence and the default terminal-semantic owner. It stops for user choice before reimplementing those semantics, adding a private adapter, or forking. This is not a prerequisite for the accepted cell-only baseline.

title: Choose the libghostty-native interaction boundary
description:
Decision: GO for a direct libghostty-native viewport and selection boundary. This decision changes no runtime contract and preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7.

Orbit keeps its existing sole libghostty terminal authority. Venus sends bounded semantic viewport and selection gestures; Orbit mutates the authoritative libghostty viewport or selection and publishes a newer complete ORBF frame. Copy text is formatted by Orbit from the terminal-owned selection and only the bounded result crosses to Venus for an explicit native clipboard action.

This is not a go for history paging. No stable row identity, epoch, anchor, retained-row page, client cache, snapshot, raw-byte parser, local fork, private adapter, or upstream change is required.
design:
Accepted public mechanisms in libghostty-vt 0.2.1:
- Terminal.scroll_viewport supports Top, Bottom, bounded Delta, and absolute Row behavior.
- Terminal.is_mouse_tracking exposes authoritative application-mouse ownership.
- Viewport grid references resolve current visible cells without long-lived external identity.
- Selection gesture APIs translate bounded press, drag, and release input into terminal selections.
- Terminal.set_selection and RenderState selected-cell data make ORBF selected styling authoritative.
- Terminal.format_selection_buf supports bounded terminal-owned plain-text extraction.

Accepted boundary:
1. Orbit decides wheel or viewport behavior from current terminal modes and owns the native viewport mutation.
2. Every accepted viewport or selection mutation produces a complete ordered ORBF frame; Venus never materializes retained history separately.
3. Selection coordinates are valid only against the current viewport and current interaction. They are not durable history identifiers.
4. A terminal mutation during an active drag cancels and resets the gesture. Successful release freezes bounded copy text immediately. Later ordinary output clears potentially remapped visual selection but may retain that immutable copy candidate until explicit copy, a new selection, resize or reflow, screen transition, detach, client loss, or exit.
5. Detach or client loss returns the viewport to Bottom and clears transient interaction state before reattachment.
6. Application mouse tracking keeps normal mouse gestures application-owned. Venus may expose a separate explicit host-selection gesture, but its native modifier policy remains consumer-owned.

Rejected boundary:
The prior history request and response plane, page tokens, row offsets, cache epochs, client page cache, stale-page recovery, and snapshot identity are deleted from the plan. The tracked-reference erase defect remains valid evidence but is irrelevant to this short-lived viewport interaction. orb-upstream-libghostty-reference-loss-dck preserves it independently.

Portability disposition: neutral terminal and protocol behavior above the existing isolated Linux platform seam. No crate change is selected.
acceptance_criteria:
1. GO: the accepted baseline uses libghostty native viewport, selection, selected-cell rendering, and selection formatting through Orbit authority.
2. ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 remain unchanged by this planning decision.
3. Complete ordered ORBF frames remain the only live presentation and reattachment authority.
4. No long-lived history identity or retained-row model crosses the Orbit and Venus boundary.
5. Application mouse tracking is decided by Orbit from authoritative terminal state; Venus does not infer terminal modes from rendered text.
6. Selection endpoints are bounded current-viewport coordinates. Mutation, resize or reflow, screen transition, detach, client loss, and exit have explicit clearing or cancellation semantics before implementation.
7. Copy text is formatted and bounded by Orbit; Venus owns only explicit user action and the native clipboard side effect.
8. orb-j0m.2 and orb-j0m.3 must index their exact user-approved contracts before production code and classify any ORBS change and Venus update order.
9. The simple complete-frame path is measured before any coalescing, paging, caching, patching, or dependency is considered.
10. orb-upstream-libghostty-reference-loss-dck is P3 deferred and is not a prerequisite.
11. No production, test, manifest, generated, protocol, contract-index, Venus, or Eon file changed in this decision.
notes:
The earlier NO-GO remains correct for client-materialized history pages: erased tracked references can silently remap under the pinned dependency. The user chose not to make that API part of the product boundary.

The new design avoids the failed identity requirement instead of compensating for it. It uses dependency-owned viewport and selection state already present in the accepted crate and keeps one complete presentation owner.
close_reason: User accepted the direct libghostty-native interaction boundary; stable history identity is not required.

title: Drive the authoritative libghostty viewport
description:
Orbit implementation child for the authoritative native history viewport.

Contract routing:
- Proposes this exact new native-viewport contract for explicit user approval: On a healthy attachment, Orbit routes each vertical-wheel message from authoritative libghostty state. Active mouse tracking sends only mouse input to the PTY; otherwise an active alternate screen with DEC private mode 1007 sends only terminal-aware cursor input; otherwise Orbit applies one row of native viewport movement. Primary movement clamps within retained history and no-history movement is an accepted no-op. Every host-owned wheel action queues Accepted followed by a strictly newer complete frame of the resulting authoritative viewport. A successful semantic key event that emits PTY bytes returns a scrolled primary viewport to the live area and queues its resulting complete frame. Client disconnection does not transfer, reconstruct, or reset viewport ownership; reattachment begins with one coherent frame of the current Orbit-owned viewport. Rejected or malformed input cannot mutate terminal state, and viewport interaction cannot block authoritative PTY processing.
- Creates and indexes that contract only after the user approves the wording; planning alone changes no contract.
- Preserves and reruns ORB-C1 through ORB-C7, especially ORB-C2 terminal authority, ORB-C4 complete ordered frames, ORB-C5 semantic input, and ORB-C7 pressure.
- Changes no ORBS or ORBF bytes and no orbit-protocol API. The known Venus consumer at c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6 already emits the required bounded Mouse and Key values, so the Orbit runtime may land first with no schema compatibility window or consumer adapter.

User-visible behavior:
The existing vertical wheel scrolls retained primary history, routes to mouse-aware applications, or follows DEC 1007 alternate-scroll behavior according to Orbit authoritative state. Scrolling down or typing terminal-producing input returns to live output. Orbit keeps the current viewport across a transient Venus disconnect and sends that coherent current view on reattachment. Venus stores no history pages, anchors, epochs, or terminal modes.
design:
Prerequisites and evidence:
orb-j0m.1 is closed. Before code, claim this Bead, record the Execution baseline, index the user-approved contract, and pass the Reference gate.
- Required before code: libghostty-vt 0.2.1 public Terminal, Screen, Mode, MouseEncoder, KeyEncoder, ScrollViewport, and Scrollbar APIs; pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 Surface.scrollCallback, Terminal.scrollViewport, PageList.scroll and scrollbar, screen switching, and key scroll-to-bottom behavior; official XTerm Control Sequences Patch 410 behavior for DEC private mode 1007.
- Comparison only: current Ghostty scroll-to-bottom and scroll action documentation.
- Rejected scope: WezTerm-style history pages or client row caches, Mosh-style history replication, and the superseded Orbit paging design.
No crate gate is expected: the standard owner loop and selected libghostty dependency expose every required mechanism.

Smallest implementation shape:
1. Keep canonical ORBS v1 unchanged. Reuse Mouse buttons Four and Five for one-row vertical wheel actions and reuse successful Key input as the native return-live trigger. Do not add Viewport, Delta, Top, Bottom, ReturnLive, page, anchor, epoch, or cache messages.
2. Route one vertical wheel in the existing owner path: if Terminal.is_mouse_tracking is true, use the existing MouseEncoder only; else if Terminal.active_screen is Alternate and Mode::ALT_SCROLL is enabled, use the existing terminal-aware KeyEncoder for one unmodified cursor-up or cursor-down press; else call Terminal.scroll_viewport with Delta(-1) for button Four or Delta(1) for button Five.
3. For the host viewport branch, queue Accepted, advance the revision once, and publish one complete ORBF frame through the existing bounded latest-frame queue even when libghostty clamps the movement. Do not query the scrollbar merely to suppress an identical boundary frame; pinned Ghostty explicitly treats clamped scroll false positives as cheap.
4. For a Key event, preserve current encoding and PTY queue admission first. Only when it emits bytes and the active screen is Primary, use the public scrollbar state to detect a non-live viewport, move it to Bottom, advance once, and queue the resulting complete frame. Empty key encodings, paste, focus, resize, horizontal wheel, and application-owned wheel input do not acquire implicit viewport policy.
5. Keep the viewport in libghostty across detach and client loss. Reattachment already extracts the current authoritative active viewport, so no disconnect hook, inactive-screen mutation, pending-reset flag, or client interaction snapshot is needed.
6. Leave output while scrolled, pruning, CSI 3 J, resize, reflow, alternate-screen switching, and viewport clamping to libghostty. Existing PTY reads continue to publish complete frames from whatever authoritative viewport libghostty exposes.
7. Existing framing, 1024-byte client reads, one wheel action per decoded message, PTY-write bound, latest-frame replacement, and 4 MiB output bound remain the pressure limits. Add no second queue or input coalescer before measurement.

First proof:
Start with one table-driven TDD routing check over primary history, top and bottom clamps, active mouse tracking, alternate screen with DEC 1007 on and off, cursor-key mode, and emitted versus empty key input. Extend one real-PTY lifecycle proof to cover retained history, output while pinned, return-live typing, clear/prune/resize/reflow, detach and coherent reattach at the same viewport, stopped-reader pressure, and final convergence. Reuse existing canonical codec checks because the protocol package must remain byte-identical. Measure rapid-wheel gesture-to-frame latency and full-frame cost before proposing coalescing or patches.

Portability disposition: neutral above the existing isolated platform seam. No new crate, upstream change, ORBS revision, or macOS blocker is expected.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact native-viewport contract in the description is user-approved and indexed before production code. Closure records its stable ID and exact proof commit.
2. Cargo manifests, Cargo.lock, ORBS v1, ORBF v1, and the public orbit-protocol API and bytes remain unchanged. The exact Venus protocol dependency remains a compatible consumer without an adapter or support window.
3. Each existing vertical-wheel message represents one bounded row. On the primary screen without mouse tracking, buttons Four and Five move through libghostty-retained history, clamp at top and live bottom, queue Accepted, and publish one strictly newer complete frame, including at a clamped boundary.
4. When libghostty mouse tracking is active, vertical and horizontal wheel input uses only the existing MouseEncoder, produces the current mode-specific PTY bytes, and does not also move or frame a host viewport.
5. On the alternate screen without mouse tracking, DEC mode 1007 enabled maps vertical wheel to one terminal-aware cursor key with correct DECCKM encoding and no host frame; mode 1007 disabled sends no PTY bytes and follows the host branch, whose no-history movement is an accepted no-op with a newer complete frame.
6. A semantic Key event returns a scrolled primary viewport to Bottom only after it produces bytes and those bytes fit the PTY queue. It queues Accepted and the newer live frame without duplicating or reordering PTY input. Empty key encodings and non-Key messages do not gain this policy.
7. Output while scrolled, history pruning, CSI 3 J, resize, reflow, and alternate-screen transitions expose only libghostty-authored state through complete ordered frames. No copied row store, stable row identity, raw-byte replay, or second terminal state exists.
8. Client disconnect leaves the Orbit-owned viewport intact. Reattachment begins with one coherent complete frame of that current viewport; scrolling or terminal-producing typing then returns live without retained client state.
9. Malformed protocol input is rejected before viewport mutation. Rapid wheel input and a stopped reader remain bounded by current per-read, PTY-write, latest-frame, and 4 MiB output limits, while PTY reads, terminal replies, cleanup, and final convergence continue.
10. One table-driven routing check and one real-PTY lifecycle proof cover the behavior above. Canonical locked Rust checks, governance, formatting, Clippy, tests, and git diff checking pass.
11. Closure records preserved ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 proof updates, the new contract proof, exact references, no-crate and compatibility dispositions, Linux environment, portability, production and test LOC, rapid-wheel latency/full-frame measurements, and remaining selection, copy, search, effects, graphics, and restart gaps.

Scope boundary:
Orbit native viewport interaction only. No selection, copy, Venus UI, explicit bottom control, page cache, search, patches, effects, resources, multiple sessions, remote transport, or restart persistence.
notes:
Accepted implementation: Orbit remains the single terminal and viewport owner. The owner loop routes ORBS v1 vertical wheel messages from current libghostty state: active mouse reporting stays with MouseEncoder; alternate screen plus DEC 1007 becomes one terminal-aware KeyEncoder cursor event; every other vertical wheel calls Terminal::scroll_viewport for one row and publishes Accepted then a newer complete frame. A byte-producing semantic Key returns a scrolled Primary viewport to Bottom only after PTY-queue admission. Viewport and revision state survive client loss with no disconnect flag, cache, row identity, replay, or second terminal owner.

Accepted proof revision: 840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0. It proves ORB-C8 and preserves and refreshes ORB-C1 through ORB-C7. The exact Venus dependency at c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6 remains byte-compatible. ORBS v1, ORBF v1, orbit-protocol, Cargo manifests, Cargo.lock, and the selected dependency graph are unchanged; no adapter or compatibility window is required.

Proof coverage: authoritative_viewport_routes_wheel_and_key_from_terminal_state covers primary up/down and top/live clamps, application mouse including horizontal wheel, DEC 1007 normal and DECCKM cursor encodings, disabled-1007 alternate no-op framing, byte-producing and empty Key behavior, PTY admission failure, and authoritative resize revision retention when bounded client output is full. authoritative_viewport_survives_detach_and_slow_reader_pressure covers pinned output, byte-identical coherent reattachment, return-live typing, CSI 3 J, pruning beyond the 1000-row limit, resize/reflow, rapid wheel input, stopped-reader pressure, release, and PTY convergence. On the accepted Linux x86_64 revision, 32 synchronous wheel round trips took 39.620976 ms and the complete ORBS frame was 12,809 bytes.

Canonical proof checks passed on the accepted revision: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace with 49 tests and zero failures; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; target/starcompass/bin/starcompass check-consumer --overlay .agent-protocols.local.md --exceptions .agent-protocols.exceptions.json --manifest .agent-protocols.json --agents AGENTS.md; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.

Owned LOC: production src/main.rs is +57 lines; co-located and lifecycle tests are +370 lines, for +427 product Rust lines. README.md records 6,454 product Rust lines and 7,219 total owned Rust lines. Fresh-eyes simplification removed 91 test lines while retaining every case and observable assertion. No direct or transitive dependency LOC was added. Portability disposition: neutral above the existing isolated Linux platform seam; no macOS blocker or support claim.

Selection, copy, search, patches, effects, graphics resources, multiple sessions, remote transport, and restart persistence remain outside ORB-C8. title: Drive authoritative selection and copy in the native viewport
description: Accepted Orbit implementation for ORB-C9 authoritative current-viewport selection and bounded copy. ORBS v2 carries revision-bound Begin, ordered Update and Finish, explicit Copy, and bounded CopiedText. Orbit owns selection resolution, selected presentation, and immutable frozen text; Venus remains responsible for pointer gesture policy, accessibility from canonical frames, and the native clipboard side effect. The breaking Orbit-first update is accepted at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757: Venus updates separately through ven-4sn, with no v1 adapter, dual support, feature probe, or compatibility window. ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 are proved at that exact revision.
design: Accepted implementation shape: the existing owner loop keeps one active anchor cell, one frozen String candidate, and whether libghostty currently presents a selection. Begin validates the exact latest frame revision and current-viewport coordinate; Update and Finish require the uninterrupted active phase. Every accepted phase resolves fresh Point::Viewport GridRefs, creates one linear libghostty Selection, reserves worst-case Accepted-plus-frame output, installs the terminal-owned selection, and publishes one newer complete frame. Finish probes libghostty plain, unwrap, and trim formatting for its required length, enforces the 1 MiB copy limit before exact allocation, then freezes the whole UTF-8 result before committing state. Copy returns only that immutable client-scoped candidate. Every non-selection terminal mutation clears the active anchor and visual selection before mutation. PTY output, viewport movement, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions preserve the frozen value because they cannot reinterpret it. A newer valid Begin, client loss, or exit clears it. ORBS v2 and ORBF v1 remain platform-neutral above the existing Linux seam. No new module, crate, manifest feature, tracked endpoint, Gesture object, pixel protocol, request table, page cache, upstream change, or clipboard owner is added.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ORB-C9 is user-approved and indexed before production code with Orbit as selection, styling, and text owner and Venus as gesture-policy, accessibility, and clipboard owner.
2. ORBS v2 remains the approved breaking Orbit-first replacement, names Venus at c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6, and has no adapter, dual support, probe, or compatibility window.
3. Begin binds to the exact latest complete-frame revision and a valid current-viewport cell; rejected input cannot mutate interaction or copy state.
4. Begin and Update use fresh libghostty viewport GridRefs and linear Selection snapshots, install the sole terminal-owned selection, and queue Accepted followed by a newer complete frame.
5. Finish formats its fresh snapshot with libghostty plain, unwrap, and trim semantics, enforces the 1 MiB bound, atomically installs the final selection and whole immutable String, then queues Accepted followed by a newer complete frame. Failure exposes no partial text.
6. Exact text is correct for forward, reverse, single-cell, wrapping, hard breaks, combining and wide graphemes, empty and erased cells, and retained rows visible in the current viewport.
7. Every non-selection terminal mutation cancels an active interaction and clears visual selection before mutation. Successfully frozen text survives later PTY output, viewport movement, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions without reinterpretation.
8. A newer valid Begin, detach or client loss, and exit clear interaction, visual selection, and frozen text without resetting the ORB-C8 viewport. Reattachment starts from that view without stale client-scoped selection state.
9. Coordinates, revision, span, formatted bytes, per-event work, storage, payloads, input, and queued output remain explicitly bounded and cannot block PTY processing or cleanup.
10. One strong codec check and one real-terminal lifecycle check cover revision binding, Unicode text, bounds, phase order, terminal-mutation clearing, immutable retention through ordinary output, alternate screen and resize, pressure, detach and reattach, client loss, and response ordering.
11. Closure records exact Orbit proof, ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 disposition, compatibility order, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, measurements, and deferred autoscroll, word or line selection, search, clipboard effects, graphics, and restart gaps.

Scope boundary: Orbit current-viewport linear cell selection and bounded plain-text copy only. No rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, word or line click selection, native clipboard access, client-side extraction, paging, search, semantic regions, effects, patches, graphics, multiple sessions, remote transport, or restart persistence.
notes:

Orbit owns one anchor, one bounded frozen String, and one visual-selection bit. Begin binds to the current complete-frame revision; every phase resolves fresh references; Finish bounds and freezes exact text before commit. The frozen value is independent of later terminal state and survives PTY output, viewport movement, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions. A newer Begin, client loss, or exit clears it. disconnect_client remains the sole client-drop cleanup owner.

title: Accept native history, scrolling, selection, and copy
description:
Final no-code cross-repository acceptance child for the native history baseline. It changes no runtime contract.

Start only after orb-j0m.5 completes its one-scenario Valgrind Memcheck hardening check against the accepted selection-capable Orbit revision and Venus ven-4sn proves its consumer against ORB-C8 at 840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0 and ORB-C9 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757. Venus is already re-primed away from the discarded page-cache design. Use the real Orbit and Venus pair; a diagnostic client, recorded frame, replay source, or Memcheck scenario cannot substitute for native interaction.

Dogfood ordinary shell output, long retained primary history, rapid wheel movement, byte-producing key return to live, wrapped Unicode and wide graphemes, current-viewport selection and copy, alternate-screen Neovim and Yazi, application mouse mode, DEC 1007 alternate scroll, resize and reflow, pruning, CSI 3 J, detach, reattach, client loss, mutation during selection, output after Finish, oversized copy, and stopped-reader pressure. Record exact revisions, environment, user-visible behavior, bounds, latency, memory, accessibility, and failure ownership.
design:
Acceptance compares the simple native-owner path with ordinary terminal behavior, not with the discarded paging architecture.

Use the exact accepted complete-frame queue and one-client boundary. ORB-C8 is already fixed: active mouse tracking sends only application mouse input; alternate screen with DEC 1007 sends only terminal-aware cursor input; all other vertical wheel input is host-owned one-row viewport movement, including an accepted no-op frame when alternate-screen history cannot move. A byte-producing key returns a scrolled primary viewport to live. Disconnect preserves the Orbit-owned viewport; reattachment projects that view.

Observe whether one local gesture round trip plus a complete frame is responsive enough. A performance miss is recorded with its smallest owner and measurement; this Bead does not authorize coalescing, patches, caching, protocol redesign, or implementation.

The accepted initial selection ceiling is current-viewport linear cells. Rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, word or line click selection, auto-copy, rich clipboard formats, and retained-history search are later choices rather than acceptance blockers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Exact Orbit and Venus proof revisions, ORB-C and VEN-C IDs, compatibility order, commands, environment, and known limitations are recorded before dogfood. Orbit includes ORB-C8 at 840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0, ORB-C9 and ORBS v2 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757, and the exact orb-j0m.5 manual Memcheck result for that selection-capable revision.
2. Primary-screen host scrolling traverses authoritative retained history and clamps or returns to live without PTY wheel bytes, stale rows, duplicated presentation, paging state, or client-owned history. A successful byte-producing key returns a scrolled primary viewport to live.
3. Active application mouse tracking is coherent in Neovim and Yazi: wheel input reaches the application and does not also move or frame a host viewport.
4. On the alternate screen without application mouse tracking, DEC 1007 enabled sends only terminal-aware cursor input; DEC 1007 disabled performs the accepted host-owned no-op and publishes its newer complete frame. Neither path invents client-owned history.
5. Output while scrolled, pruning, CSI 3 J, resize and reflow preserve one libghostty-owned viewport and complete-frame convergence. Disconnect does not reset or transfer viewport ownership; reattachment begins with the current Orbit-owned view.
6. Cell-granular selection and explicit copy return exact authoritative plain text across current and stale start revisions, forward and reverse drags, wrapping, hard breaks, Unicode, combining and wide graphemes, and retained rows visible in the viewport.
7. A non-selection mutation during an active selection cancels cleanly. After Finish, terminal output, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions clear stale visual selection without changing the frozen copy candidate. A newer valid Begin, client loss, or exit clears that candidate without resetting the ORB-C8 viewport.
8. Gesture-to-frame and copy latency, full-frame and copy bytes, CPU, memory, input work, queued output, and stopped-reader behavior are measured under rapid interaction and long output. Measurements do not become broader performance claims, and the single Memcheck scenario does not become a general memory-safety claim.
9. Accessibility exposes the accepted viewport, authoritative selected styling, copy result or failure, and reconnect state from the same frame and interaction results used visually.
10. Every confirmed defect is assigned to exactly one Orbit or Venus owner with the exact compatibility sequence. No product code, test, manifest, adapter, dependency, trace format, page cache, or upstream change is made here.
11. The result records one outcome: accepted for Eon dogfood, or orb-j0m remains open with one named owner gap. Search and deferred selection enhancements cannot block this result.
12. Parent orb-j0m reconciles owner and consumer proofs, contracts, Memcheck evidence, measurements, portability, LOC, and remaining search, semantic-region, effects, graphics, restart, multi-session, and remote limitations before closure.

Scope boundary:
No implementation. No search, semantic regions, agent observer, effects, graphics, patch protocol, page cache, workspace, distribution, multiple sessions, remote transport, or restart persistence.
notes:
Venus ven-4sn is re-primed against the accepted host-owned viewport, history, selection, and copy boundary at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757. It keeps no page cache, epoch, stable anchor, row token, or client-owned terminal selection. It remains deferred until orb-j0m.5 closes, then becomes the next implementation frontier.

orb-j0m.5 is an Orbit-only P2 hardening prerequisite after the selection proof and before this acceptance. Its one direct Memcheck lifecycle checks the integrated Rust, libghostty, libc, process, and descriptor seam; it does not replace real Venus interaction, accessibility, performance measurement, or dogfood.

The deferred upstream tracked-reference correction is independent and absent from the acceptance prerequisites.

title: Prove one Orbit lifecycle under Valgrind Memcheck
description:
Repository-hardening slice with no new user-visible behavior or product contract. After the accepted ORB-C9 selection proof, run one deterministic real Orbit server lifecycle under Valgrind Memcheck across the Rust, libghostty C ABI and Zig implementation, and direct libc PTY and socket seam.

The scenario starts one actual Orbit server and child process, attaches a protocol-faithful client, drives representative VT output, resizes, scrolls, selects and copies, detaches, reattaches, and exits the child and server cleanly. It checks memory access, initialization, deallocation, heap retention, and file-descriptor lifecycle at the integrated boundary that ordinary Rust checks cannot observe.

Contract routing:
- Changes no product contract, wire behavior, runtime policy, dependency, supported platform, or proof status by itself.
- Hardens the exact accepted implementation surfaces supporting ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C4 through ORB-C9. Reconfirm the accepted IDs and proof revisions at activation.
- Runs after orb-j0m.3 and before orb-j0m.4 cross-repository acceptance, so the exact selection-capable Orbit revision is checked before dogfood.

Scope:
- One Linux-only deterministic end-to-end lifecycle and one direct Valgrind Memcheck invocation.
- The exact pinned libghostty-vt and libghostty-vt-sys build, underlying Ghostty revision, Rust toolchain, Zig toolchain, Valgrind version, optimization/debug-info mode, command, suppressions, elapsed time, and result.
- Fatal memory errors, definite or indirect leaks, and leaked or invalid file descriptors.
- Non-fatal reporting and classification of possibly lost and still-reachable allocations.
- The smallest reusable local command or script only if direct invocation cannot remain reproducible without it.

Out of scope:
- Running the complete Cargo suite under Valgrind, per-push or scheduled CI, a CI matrix, macOS Valgrind support, cargo-valgrind or another wrapper dependency, ASan or Miri implementation, performance claims, fuzzing, coverage, product changes, a test-only product mode, a new binary, or broad suppression import.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Start only after orb-j0m.3 closes with an accepted proof-bearing revision. Re-read the exact ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 index and record an Execution baseline for this one hardening issue before any tracked test, script, suppression, workflow, Nix, or documentation edit.
2. Pass the Reference gate before edits. Required primary evidence: the exact Valgrind Memcheck and core-option manuals; the exact pinned libghostty-vt, libghostty-vt-sys, and Ghostty sources exercised by the scenario; and the current Orbit lifecycle harness and unsafe platform seam. Inspect Ghostty Valgrind and suppression mechanisms only if the first unsuppressed run reports an upstream or runtime-owned finding. Record the exact selected tool and source identities plus relevant licenses.
3. Keep the user-selected tool shape: invoke the Valgrind executable directly. Prefer an already supplied system or Nix tool and add no Cargo wrapper, Rust dependency, framework, product binary, or installation automation. Stop for user choice before adding hosted CI, a Nix package surface, installer logic, or another dynamic-analysis tool.
4. Build the exact accepted Orbit and pinned libghostty artifacts with useful debug symbols. Record optimization mode and prove that the actual yazelix-orbit server process, not only Cargo or the test harness, runs under Memcheck. Prefer direct server wrapping; use narrowly scoped child tracing only if necessary and prevent unrelated shells or helpers from contaminating the result.
5. Reuse the existing protocol and lifecycle helpers where possible. Drive one bounded scenario through server start, real child PTY output with representative VT state, client attach, resize, host viewport scroll, authoritative selection and copy, detach, reattach, child exit, server exit, socket cleanup, and process reaping. Do not run unrelated tests.

title: Advertise the Eon terminal identity
description:
User-approved correction for the orb-j0m.4 dogfood gap. Orbit currently sets TERM=xterm-ghostty for every PTY child, but the accepted development and dogfood environment does not install that terminfo entry, so clear and other terminfo consumers fail.

Create ORB-C10: every Orbit PTY child advertises TERM=eon, and the accepted launch environment supplies the repository-owned eon terminfo entry. Keep the initial capability profile conservative by inheriting the installed xterm-256color record while Orbit continues to use libghostty and COLORTERM=truecolor. This is a PTY child-environment behavior change, not an ORBS or ORBF protocol change; Venus remains unchanged.

Scope: one two-line terminfo source, the existing TERM assignment, the minimum current launch documentation, focused real-PTY proof, the contract index, and required LOC scorecard update. No dependency, build framework, runtime installer, compatibility alias, configuration surface, terminal-profile abstraction, packaging system, remote support, or Venus change.
design:
Contract and implementation shape:

- ORB-C10 consumer: every program spawned inside an Orbit-owned PTY. Trigger: PTY child spawn. Result: TERM=eon resolves through the accepted launch environment to a compiled Eon terminfo entry whose initial capabilities are the conservative xterm-256color baseline; COLORTERM remains truecolor. Important failure: launch is not accepted if eon cannot be resolved or clear fails.
- Source owner: terminfo/eon.terminfo. Orbit owns the advertised identity in src/platform.rs. Eon distribution will later install the same source into its runtime closure; this Bead adds no packaging surface.
- Required before code: pinned Ghostty a887df42 terminfo identity and build behavior; installed ncurses tic/terminfo primary documentation and xterm-256color entry. Comparison only: the absent xterm-ghostty entry and a no-custom-name fallback. Rejected scope: copying Ghostty's generated capability table, runtime materialization, custom feature deltas, remote propagation, configuration, and aliases.
- First falsifying check: compile the source with tic into an isolated directory, resolve eon with infocmp, launch a real Orbit PTY with that TERMINFO directory, and prove TERM=eon plus a successful clear sequence.
- Platform disposition: isolated Linux terminfo dependency; macOS packaging is unproved, but the source format and tic workflow are portable. No ORBS/ORBF or Venus compatibility change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. terminfo/eon.terminfo contains one Eon entry inheriting xterm-256color, with no duplicated capability table.
2. Orbit sets TERM=eon for every PTY child and keeps COLORTERM=truecolor.
3. tic -x compiles the source into an isolated terminfo directory; infocmp resolves eon and shows the inherited baseline.
4. A real Orbit-owned PTY launched with that directory reports TERM=eon, clear exits successfully, and the shell remains usable.
5. README documents the current one-command terminfo installation before running Orbit. The later Eon package remains explicitly responsible for installing the same entry rather than gaining a speculative packaging implementation here.
6. docs/CONTRACTS.md records ORB-C10 and exact proof status without changing ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 or the Orbit/Venus protocol boundary.
7. No dependency, build script, installer, runtime extraction, alias set, configuration, protocol, Venus, remote, or compatibility layer is added.
8. README LOC scorecard reflects tracked handwritten project files, and canonical Rust, governance, clippy, terminfo, real-PTY, and git-diff checks pass.
9. Closure records the exact proof-bearing commit only after the accepted revision exists; until then evidence remains candidate.
notes: User decision 2026-08-07: the repository is private; adopt the Eon terminal identity now rather than preserving xterm-ghostty compatibility history. Ponytail shape selected: two source lines, one existing Rust literal changed, standard tic, and no framework.

title: Transfer rich terminal graphics through a bounded resource plane
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved graphics-resource contract and explicit ORB-C6 change before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and every accepted predecessor contract while extending the cross-repository presentation boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus graphics consumer contract and an explicit compatible-or-breaking update order. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

ORBF v1 explicitly advertises Kitty graphics as unsupported even though authoritative libghostty state can contain image resources and placements. Repeating image bytes in complete frames would be wasteful and unsafe; ignoring them leaves a permanent rich-presentation gap for Yazi previews, image tools, and graphical terminal applications.

## Evidence

- `src/presentation.rs:140-146` advertises hyperlink support and Kitty graphics unsupported.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:130-135` carries the capability bit but no resource or placement representation.
- `tests/formatter_attachment.rs:224-237` proves authoritative Kitty image state is not recoverable through formatter bootstrap.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27,65-70` records ORB-C6 as proved with graphics explicitly outside version 1.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` routes capability-negotiated rich resources independently of frames and effect ordering.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:77-86` records WezTerm's separate image-cell hydration as relevant protocol evidence.

## Scope

In scope:
- Capability negotiation and a bounded resource/placement plane owned by Orbit.
- Compare epoch-scoped opaque resource IDs with content-addressed resources; select the smaller correct identity and cache contract.
- Strict type, dimension, byte, chunk, count, lifetime, placement, eviction, missing-resource, reconnect, alternate-screen, resize, and pressure semantics.
- Venus GPU upload/cache/placement through a separately owned consumer proof.
- One real Kitty graphics producer such as a Yazi/image preview in dogfood.

Out of scope:
- A general multimedia framework, sixel unless separately chosen, video/animation breadth beyond the first contract, client terminal emulation, image history persistence across Orbit restart, remote CDN/storage, or embedding bytes in every frame.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, approve and index the graphics-resource contract plus the ORB-C6 change; classify the wire revision and every known Venus consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact libghostty-vt 0.2.1/current published graphics resource and placement APIs; the Kitty graphics protocol; WezTerm's resource hydration/cache mechanism at the routed commit; and one real producer used by Eon such as Yazi. Reject unrelated terminal/mux architecture.
3. First prove the public libghostty surface exposes enough resource bytes, placement, lifecycle, scrolling, and generation state. Stop before forks or binding extensions.
4. Compare session/epoch-local IDs against cryptographic content IDs. Content hashing must remove enough retransmission/deduplication complexity to justify its dependency and CPU cost.
5. Keep frames small by referring to placements/resources. Define announce/chunk/request/evict/missing/resync semantics and strict quotas before the happy path.
6. Orbit owns resource interpretation and lifetime. Venus owns validated GPU resources and cache eviction but cannot infer missing placements or decode terminal protocol.
7. Land the protocol/Orbit proof first, then a separate Venus GPU proof and real-program dogfood.

Dependency decision: no hashing, image-decoding, compression, chunking, or cache crate is selected. Every direct or architecture-shaping choice requires the Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral resource protocol; GPU formats, upload, and platform limits stay in Venus.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the exact published libghostty API cannot expose the required resource/placement state.
- Stop for user choice before a binding extension, fork, alternative terminal engine, breaking wire revision, or compatibility window.
- Stop if quotas cannot prevent allocation/decompression/resource bombs before work begins.
- Stop if the first useful program requires a broader graphics protocol than the approved Kitty slice.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The graphics-resource contract and ORB-C6 change are approved and indexed before implementation, with exact Venus compatibility/update order.
2. A negotiated client either receives the supported graphics contract or an explicit unsupported capability; presentation never silently drops authoritative placements.
3. Resource identity, announcements, bytes/chunks, placements, scrolling, resize, alternate screen, deletion, eviction, missing resources, reconnect, and resync have deterministic epoch/revision semantics.
4. Resource count, dimensions, encoded/decoded bytes, chunks, outstanding requests, cache memory, and queue pressure are bounded before allocation.
5. Complete frames refer to resources without repeating full payloads, and a slow/missing-resource consumer cannot block PTY processing or corrupt later presentation.
6. Focused tests cover malformed metadata, oversized resources, duplicate IDs/content, chunk gaps, eviction, out-of-order placement/resource arrival, reconnect, alternate screen, resize, and client failure.
7. A separate Venus proof consumes the exact Orbit revision, validates uploads, renders placement geometry, survives GPU/cache eviction, and requests/resyncs missing resources without terminal inference.
8. Real Linux dogfood demonstrates at least one accepted Kitty graphics producer, including scrolling and detach/reattach.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records compatibility, crate decision, resource measurements, portability, LOC, proof revisions, security bounds, and unsupported formats.
notes:
Priority P3: strategically important for avoiding a text-grid ceiling, but materially larger and riskier than hyperlinks, effects, history, semantics, accessibility, workspace composition, and the observer.

Blocked by orb-bi4.7. It is independent of patch optimization and ordered effects; do not couple those planes merely because both change the protocol.

Rejected alternatives: embedding image bytes in each frame, client parsing Kitty escapes, adopting a general image framework before one producer is proved, assuming content hashes are automatically simpler, unbounded resource caching, or claiming formatter/bootstrap restoration.

Planning estimate: effort L; implementation risk HIGH (resource security, cache/lifetime semantics, GPU consumption, and compatibility); confidence MED until the published libghostty graphics surface is proved sufficient.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. If selected after graduation, create children for: (1) a research spike proving the exact published libghostty graphics API is sufficient; (2) the resource identity, wire, quota, eviction, and compatibility decision; (3) Orbit-owned bounded resource transfer; (4) a separate Venus GPU cache and placement consumer; and (5) real-producer dogfood and acceptance. A failed API spike stops before a fork, binding extension, dependency, or alternate terminal engine.

title: Separate coalescible terminal state from ordered effects
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved effects contract before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 while changing the client-facing ORBS boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus consumer contract and exact compatible-or-breaking update order. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

ORBF complete frames are intentionally replaceable latest state. Bells, clipboard writes, notifications, and similar terminal effects are ordered events and cannot inherit frame coalescing without silent loss or duplication. Conversely title, working directory, and latest progress are state and should not become an append-only event log. Terminal-generated PTY responses are a third class and must remain on the authoritative Orbit-to-PTY path rather than entering either client plane.

## Evidence

- docs/RATIONALE.md records distinct Snapshot, History, Effects, Resources, and Actions planes and assigns ordered effects to Orbit.
- README.md identifies a separate ordered effect stream as the preferred later direction requiring a user-approved decision.
- src/main.rs:140-154 installs the sole authoritative on_pty_write callback in the current owner loop.
- libghostty-vt and libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1 pin Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. Its C bridge always installs the device-attributes trampoline; without a custom callback it returns default attributes, and the terminal encodes DA1, DA2, and DA3 replies through writePty. Orbit therefore already captures those default replies through on_pty_write.
- crates/protocol/src/session.rs has no bell, clipboard, or notification server message.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md proves ordered frames and bounded client pressure but not effect delivery.

## Scope

In scope:
- Classify terminal outputs into coalescible state, ordered effects, terminal-generated PTY responses, and unsupported capabilities.
- Add bounded effect identity, ordering, delivery, overflow, detach, reattach, and version-mismatch semantics.
- Capture supported libghostty effects without blocking its synchronous callbacks.
- Keep default DA1, DA2, and DA3 responses on the existing authoritative PTY-response path. A custom advertised terminal identity or capability set is a separate product-policy choice, not an effect.
- Keep clipboard and native-notification policy in the highest owner with platform/user context; Orbit owns terminal interpretation and bounded transport.
- Coordinate an Orbit protocol/runtime proof followed by a separate Venus consumer proof.

Out of scope:
- Snapshot-plus-patch optimization, full history, graphics resources, remote delivery, durable event logging, notification history, custom terminal identity policy, or terminal effects replayed after an unobserved disconnect.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Add the user-approved effects contract before code and classify the ORBS change as compatible or breaking for every known Venus consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: the exact then-current libghostty effects and callback source, Ghostty BEL and OSC 52 behavior, notification and progress protocols where exposed, and one exact structured-terminal comparison such as WezTerm. Reject their unrelated multiplexer and UI scope.
3. Classify every output before adding a callback or message. Treat current title, CWD, and progress as latest state; treat bell, clipboard write, notification, and attention requests as ordered effects only when the authoritative engine exposes them; retain engine-generated query replies on on_pty_write.
4. DA1, DA2, and DA3 are terminal-generated PTY responses under ORB-C2. The pinned 0.2.1 bridge supplies default attributes when no custom on_device_attributes callback is registered and emits the encoded response through on_pty_write. Do not add a second DA encoder, client message, or effect. Register on_device_attributes only after a separately approved terminal-identity or advertised-capability policy requires non-default values.
5. Keep effect callback work bounded and nonblocking. Copy only validated bounded payloads into the Orbit owner loop.
6. Define event IDs, revision association, acknowledgements only where they serve a contract, and explicit behavior for queue pressure, disconnect, reconnect, and gaps. Never silently coalesce an ordered effect.
7. Land the canonical protocol and Orbit proof first. A separate Venus Bead then consumes the exact proof and owns native delivery and permission UX.

Dependency decision: prefer the existing standard library and libghostty APIs. Any direct crate or feature expansion requires the Crate gate before manifest edits.

Portability disposition: neutral effect values and ordering; clipboard, notification, and desktop delivery remain isolated Venus/platform concerns.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if libghostty lacks the required public callback or state API; record the exact missing surface.
- Stop if a synchronous callback would require blocking on Venus or user input.
- Stop for user choice before custom terminal identity or capability advertisement, any breaking protocol revision, or a compatibility window.
- Stop if bounded pressure cannot preserve the selected per-kind semantics without explicit failure.

Comparison-only evidence: Canario RioEngine.swift at Rio 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 immediately writes librio clipboard callbacks to NSPasteboard. Treat that as the concrete policy-coupling failure the Orbit/Venus split must avoid, not as accepted clipboard behavior or a required architecture.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The effects contract is approved and indexed before implementation, and all affected ORB-C contracts plus known Venus consumers have an explicit compatibility and update plan.
2. One contract table classifies each supported output as coalescible state, ordered effect, terminal-generated PTY response, or unsupported capability with exactly one owner.
3. DA1, DA2, and DA3 remain single authoritative terminal-generated PTY responses through the existing on_pty_write path. The proof checks the exact dependency version with no custom device-attributes callback and adds no client effect, duplicate encoder, or custom advertised identity. Any non-default identity or capability policy stops for separate user approval.
4. Interleaved frames and effects preserve authoritative order while complete frames may still coalesce; no effect is silently duplicated, reordered, or dropped.
5. Slow, detached, failed, and reconnecting clients have bounded deterministic effect behavior. Overflow or a delivery gap is explicit.
6. Clipboard payloads, notifications, and other attacker-controlled data have strict type and byte bounds; callbacks never block the terminal owner loop.
7. A focused protocol and owner-loop check covers frame coalescing around effects, callback reentrancy assumptions, disconnect, overflow, and version mismatch.
8. A separately owned Venus consumer proves native delivery and permission UX against the exact Orbit proof before the end-to-end feature is accepted.
9. Canonical locked Rust checks and git diff --check pass; proof revisions, changelog, dependency, portability, LOC, and remaining unsupported effects are recorded.
notes:
Priority P1: this is a correctness foundation and unlocks later clipboard, command-finished notification, progress, session-dashboard, and accessibility-alert behavior.

Blocked by orb-bi4.7. That gate is transitively behind hardening, Eon dogfood, and the explicit Orbit/Venus graduation decision.

Pinned discovery on 2026-08-07: libghostty-vt and libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1 use Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. terminal/c/terminal.zig always installs deviceAttributesTrampoline; a missing custom callback returns default Attributes. stream_terminal.zig reportDeviceAttributes encodes the matching primary, secondary, or tertiary response and calls writePty, which reaches the Rust on_pty_write callback. This is source evidence for classification, not a new accepted Orbit runtime proof.

Rejected alternatives: putting effects inside replaceable frames, routing DA replies through the client effect plane, adding a second device-attributes encoder, replaying an unbounded event log, blocking libghostty callbacks on native UI, letting Venus reinterpret escape sequences, or selecting an async/event-bus crate before the existing owner loop is measured.

Planning estimate: effort L; implementation risk HIGH for ordered delivery, synchronous callbacks, security, and cross-repository compatibility; confidence HIGH in the need and ownership split.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. If orb-bi4.7 selects this frontier, create independently provable children for: (1) the effects classification, contract, and compatibility decision; (2) the smallest Orbit ordered-effect plane proving one user-approved effect, with BEL the default candidate rather than implied scope; (3) the separate Venus consumer proof; and (4) each additional security- or permission-sensitive effect class only when the user chooses it. Keep Orbit producer, Venus consumer, and cross-repository acceptance in separate runs.

title: Transport bounded terminal clipboard writes to the attached client
description:
Contract: introduce ORB-C11. When the authoritative terminal parses an OSC 52 or normalized equivalent write, Orbit emits one bounded ordered clipboard-write message to the currently attached ORBS client. Orbit owns interpretation and transport; Venus owns native clipboard policy and delivery. Detached writes are not retained or replayed. Unsupported representations, embedded NUL, clears, and payloads above the existing 1 MiB copy bound are rejected before admission.

Compatibility: this is an owner-first breaking ORBS v2 to v3 replacement. Existing accepted messages retain their layouts, but the exact revision advances because current Venus cannot consume the new server message. Orbit proves v3 first; a separate Venus bead and run must consume its exact proof before Eonova acceptance. No adapter, dual decoder, or compatibility window.

Scope: existing libghostty callback, one plain-text clipboard write effect, existing bounded non-coalescing output queue, exact protocol and real-PTY proof. No native clipboard access, readback, permissions UI, BEL, notification, replay log, generic effects framework, or new dependency.
design: Use libghostty-vt 0.2.1 on_clipboard_write and the existing Orbit owner loop. Admit only exactly one non-empty text/plain representation whose UTF-8 bytes are at most MAX_COPY_BYTES and contain no NUL; preserve its normalized standard, selection, or primary destination. Copy admitted writes into a count-and-byte-bounded FIFO only while a negotiated ORBS client is attached. After each PTY read, queue every effect as a non-coalescible ServerMessage before the resulting coalescible frame. An effect handoff or client-output overflow disconnects the client, making the delivery gap explicit; detached writes are denied and never retained. Advance the canonical session protocol atomically to v3; preserve all earlier message layouts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ORB-C11 is indexed before code and records the breaking v3 producer-first update order.
2. The canonical codec round-trips a destination plus UTF-8 text and rejects oversize or invalid payloads.
3. A real PTY OSC 52 write reaches the attached client exactly once and in queue order without becoming a frame.
4. Detached, unsupported, clear, binary or NUL, oversize, and full-output-queue writes are not retained or replayed; the synchronous callback stays bounded and nonblocking.
5. Existing ORB-C1 through ORB-C10 behavior remains covered and locked Rust checks pass.
6. The proof commit, references, remaining Venus consumer gap, LOC scorecard, and changelog disposition are recorded; br is flushed.
notes:
Accepted result: ORBS v3 Orbit producer proof 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174 implements ORB-C11. Orbit owns terminal interpretation and ordered bounded transport; Venus remains the sole owner of native clipboard policy and delivery. The breaking v2-to-v3 update has no adapter, dual decoder, feature probe, or compatibility window. ORB-C1 through ORB-C10 remain covered.

Implementation: reuse libghostty-vt 0.2.1 on_clipboard_write, the synchronous owner loop, and OutputQueue. PendingClipboardWrites owns the negotiated-client gate, 64-entry FIFO, cumulative 1 MiB bound, and terminal overflow state. It admits one non-empty UTF-8 text/plain representation with a valid standard, selection, or primary destination. Effects queue before the same PTY-turn frame. Detached writes return Denied and are never retained; handoff or output pressure disconnects instead of silently dropping an admitted effect.

Safety and dependencies: Cargo metadata and the dependency graph are unchanged. The pinned safe binding is unsound for a null zero-length clear and binary-safe non-UTF-8 data, so Orbit uses one compile-checked raw-pointer seam for exact libghostty-vt 0.2.1, validates pointers, bounds, MIME bytes, destination, UTF-8, and NUL before allocation, and never calls the unsafe contents iterator. Remove the seam when the binding exposes a safe byte-oriented view.

Proof: focused canonical-codec, callback admission, output-pressure, and real-PTY tests cover valid normalized destinations, invalid and oversize values, terminal batch pressure, detached denial, ordered delivery before the same-turn frame, and exactly once through the final Exited sentinel. Verification at the proof revision passed cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace with 54 tests; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; Starcompass check-consumer; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.

LOC and disposition: product Rust and tests 7,564; governance Rust 765; total owned Rust 8,329; terminfo 2; total implementation source 8,331. Protocol package 3,228 lines: 2,195 production and 1,033 tests. The accepted changelog entry and contract index name the proof revision. Protocol and owner-loop behavior remain platform-neutral.

Remaining separately owned work: Venus at 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832 consumes ORBS v2, so native delivery and Eonova runtime acceptance remain open. Pinned libghostty allocates OSC 52 parser storage before the callback; bounding that pre-existing allocation requires a separate upstream allocator or binding decision. Clears, empty, invalid UTF-8 or NUL text, multiple or non-text representations, reads, BEL, notifications, replay, remote transport, and native permission UX remain unsupported.
close_reason: Accepted ORBS v3 Orbit producer proof 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174; all local checks pass. Venus consumption and runtime acceptance remain separate.

Detached writes are denied and not replayed. Handoff or output pressure disconnects the client rather than silently coalescing an effect. comments.text:
Reference-gate revision after the first negative check

The actual OSC 52 clear check aborts inside libghostty-vt 0.2.1 before Orbit code can reject it: ClipboardWrite::contents calls slice::from_raw_parts with the C ABI null contents pointer and zero length. The bundled Ghostty test explicitly requires null plus length zero for clears. Current libghostty-rs master 1f135a350c85a44711e6a66d8ce7344a874489a8 on 2026-08-11 retains the same unsafe construction, and crates.io has no release beyond 0.2.1.

Rejected: shipping the crash; parsing or stripping OSC 52 in Orbit; vendoring or forking the binding in this producer bead; mutating Cargo registry source; or adding another terminal parser. Chosen bounded workaround: because pinned ClipboardWrite 0.2.1 is exactly one non-zero-sized raw-pointer field plus PhantomData, use a compile-checked transmute of a clone to inspect only the raw contents_len before calling the otherwise safe iterator. The transmute cannot compile if the wrapper ceases to be pointer-sized. Keep the existing exact dependency pin and remove the workaround when the binding exposes a safe clear or length query. The clear regression remains in the focused test.

comments.text:
Fresh-eyes and simplification pass (pre-edit)

Confirmed regression risk: libghostty-vt 0.2.1 ClipboardWrite::contents is unsafe for both a null zero-length clear and arbitrary binary decoded data: it constructs a slice from a null pointer for clears, then ClipboardContent::from_raw calls from_utf8_unchecked despite the ABI documenting binary-safe bytes. The candidate avoided only the clear crash and could still create an invalid Rust str from OSC 52 binary input.

Chosen root fix: retain the exact pinned wrapper-pointer seam already required for clears, but inspect the single raw ffi::ClipboardContent directly, compare the MIME as bytes, reject null/empty/invalid UTF-8/NUL/oversize data, and only then allocate an owned String. Never call ClipboardWrite::contents. This changes malformed binary input from undefined behavior to InvalidData while preserving all accepted ORB-C11 behavior. No dependency, parser, fork, or public surface is added.

Isomorphism card for the accompanying state cleanup:
- Observable behavior: callback admission remains enabled only for one negotiated non-closing client; detached writes remain denied; admitted writes, bounds, order, disconnect-on-pressure, and protocol bytes are unchanged.
- Exact preserved errors: Denied while detached; Unsupported for clear/multiple/non-text; InvalidData for empty/NUL/oversize and now invalid UTF-8; Busy for pending pressure.
- Ordering/state invariants: the gate is refreshed once at the same owner-loop point; one FIFO preserves callback order; publish still precedes the same PTY-turn frame; detach/pressure clears all pending state.
- Resource/lifetime constraints: one synchronous callback; 64 writes and 1 MiB total; no I/O or blocking; callback-borrowed bytes copied only after validation.
- Proof: focused callback regression plus real-PTY ordering, then the complete locked Rust/governance/consumer suite.

Simplification candidate accepted: move the enabled gate into PendingClipboardWrites, removing a second Rc<Cell<bool>> and the capture parameter while preserving the same refresh point. Rejected VecDeque-to-Vec and publish-helper reshaping: they remove no owner or dependency and make failure-path draining less direct.
