title: Decide whether Orbit has outgrown its owned event loop
description: Trigger this decision only when a measured Orbit contract failure, required integration, or accepted scale expansion shows that the owned synchronous poll/event loop is no longer the smallest correct execution shape. This planning and crate decision changes no product contract by itself.
design: Keep the current owned synchronous/event-loop design unless evidence demonstrates a concrete limitation. At the gate, compare Asupersync, Tokio, smol, and an owned synchronous/event-loop design at exact releases or commits. Inspect the routed primary sources before choosing code shape. Evaluate task ownership, cancellation and shutdown-to-quiescence, I/O and signal integration, deterministic schedule or replay testing, backpressure, project-owned LOC, normal and build dependency graphs, toolchain and Nix cost, license and security posture, macOS feasibility, migration risk, and ecosystem constraints from required crates. A reference using a runtime does not select it. Stop for user approval before manifest or production changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The trigger names the measured contract failure, integration requirement, or accepted scale pressure; absent one, close or keep this decision deferred with the owned loop retained.
2. The Execution baseline and Reference gate state that the bead changes no product contract unless the user separately approves a contract change.
3. The Crate gate compares exact Asupersync, Tokio, smol, and owned synchronous/event-loop candidates without padding or preselection.
4. Focused proofs measure any disputed cancellation, shutdown, deterministic-test, I/O, backpressure, LOC, dependency, build, or portability claim.
5. The decision records selected and rejected shapes, failure conditions, migration and rollback plan, first contract check, owned-LOC estimate, dependency footprint, and macOS disposition.
6. No manifest, runtime architecture, compatibility surface, or async abstraction changes before explicit user approval.
7. docs/CRATES.md and the affected ORB-C proof routing are updated only if a runtime choice is accepted and implemented.
notes:
Reference routing: docs/REFERENCES.md#execution-runtime-gate. Required at activation: Asupersync, Tokio, smol, and the then-current owned loop, each at an exact identity. FrankenTerm supplies required session/recovery/transport/failure semantics; FrankenTUI supplies deterministic rendering-transition and test-architecture evidence where the runtime affects publication; Process Triage supplies process-lifecycle and staged-action evidence. This is not a request to adopt an async runtime.

## Activation boundary

This remains a conditional runtime decision, not an implementation unit. Without a measured trigger, keep it deferred. If a runtime is selected, authorize a separate implementation Bead rather than changing the manifest or event loop inside this question.

title: Expose phased bounded read-only terminal observation for Eon agents
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved observer contract and explicit ORB-C3 change before implementation; this planning epic reserves no permanent ORB-C ID.
- Requires an Eon-owned authorization and session-selection contract before product exposure.
- The minimum visible-state observer consumes already accepted live presentation and lifecycle authority. It does not require retained-history search or semantic command regions.
- Later enrichment may consume exact accepted history and semantic-region contracts without changing the minimum proof into a durable transcript.
- Planning changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

Why:
Agents need bounded authoritative terminal context without hijacking the interactive client, scraping pixels or turning Venus frames into a log. Orbit already owns the live screen, title, CWD, active screen, revision and session lifecycle. The previous all-or-nothing plan delayed even minimum observation behind advanced history and semantic work.

Phases:
1. Minimum observer: explicitly authorized local read-only queries for session and process lifecycle, current visible text projection, title, CWD, active screen and exact revision. Text is explicitly lossy.
2. Enrichment: bounded history and last authoritative semantic command or output only after their owner contracts are accepted.

Out of scope:
Synthetic input, mutating actions, process control, provider-status inference, durable transcripts, arbitrary shell execution, remote or MCP exposure, automatic secret redaction, raw PTY or ORBF access, multiple interactive clients and bypassing the owner loop.
design:
1. Begin only after graduation and orb-bi4.7 selects agent-workspace or observation work as the single frontier. Approve the observer contract, scoped ORB-C3 change, Eon policy contract and exact cross-repository update order before code.
2. At activation split this epic into an Eon authorization/security decision, minimum Orbit observer owner, Eon capability consumer, adversarial acceptance, and later enriched observer children. The enriched child alone depends on accepted history and semantic regions.
3. Required reference evidence for the minimum phase: exact accepted Orbit contracts; exact current Herdr socket/read and agent-observation mechanisms; VS Code Agent Host; one local agent-terminal observer such as Wave or Open Terminal; FrankenTerm lifecycle/security boundaries; and relevant local Unix credential APIs. References are not dependencies by implication.
4. Define a distinct observer role and handshake. It never claims the one interactive attachment, sends input or resize, receives raw terminal bytes or obtains process-control authority.
5. Orbit owns the bounded projection and attaches session identity, revision, projection kind, source and lossy labeling. It exposes semantic or history values only from later accepted owner contracts.
6. Eon owns user consent, AgentRun and session selection, capability issuance, expiry and revocation. Orbit enforces the chosen local capability at its boundary.
7. Bound observers, queries, rows, bytes, response time, retained storage, cancellation and rate. Observer pressure cannot delay PTY mutation, presentation or cleanup.
8. Prove denial, expiry, revocation and pressure before product integration. Prefer the existing local transport/codec and standard library; any new auth, serialization, async or capability dependency requires the crate gate.
9. Keep Eon mutating actions in astra-db8.9. MCP may later adapt an accepted capability surface but is not part of either observer phase.

Stop if authorization has no single owner, minimum observation weakens interactive semantics, sensitive content can be read without explicit capability, pressure affects the owner loop, or the design requires a durable log, remote server or generic plugin framework.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Graduation and orb-bi4.7 selection precede implementation. The observer contract, scoped ORB-C3 change, Eon policy contract and update order are approved and indexed first.
2. The minimum phase does not depend on history or semantic-region implementation. One interactive Venus client remains the only input-capable attachment.
3. Authorized minimum queries return bounded session identity, process or session lifecycle, title, CWD, active screen, exact revision and explicitly lossy current visible text.
4. Observers cannot send terminal input, resize, lifecycle or process-control actions and cannot receive raw PTY bytes, ORBF frames or hidden terminal internals.
5. Unauthorized, expired, revoked, malformed, oversized, stale and cancelled queries fail deterministically without revealing terminal content.
6. Observer count, outstanding work, rows, bytes, memory, time and rate are bounded; slow observers cannot disturb PTY processing, Venus or cleanup.
7. Deterministic checks cover concurrent interactive and observer access, authorization, expiry, revocation, revision consistency, disconnect, pressure, child exit and Orbit shutdown.
8. A separate Eon proof demonstrates explicit user-controlled AgentRun and session authorization against the exact Orbit revision.
9. Later enriched observation adds bounded history or semantic command/output only after their exact accepted contracts and cannot alter the minimum API into a transcript or guessed provider-state model.
10. Read-only observation remains separate from Eon mutating actions, provider integrations, MCP, plugins, remote transport and redaction claims.
11. Closure records security model, compatibility, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, exact proofs, pressure measurements and excluded control or remote scope.
notes:
Priority P1 after graduation because agents are strategically central to Eon. The minimum observer no longer depends on orb-3gf. Later semantic enrichment remains conceptually gated by orb-3gf and history but does not block the first useful read-only slice.

Rejected alternatives: screen capture or OCR as authority, handing agents Venus frames, an always-on transcript database, unpermissioned local reads, synthetic keystrokes, output scraping as provider status, general remote or MCP exposure and claims of automatic secret redaction.

Planning estimate remains large for the complete epic because authorization, sensitive data and pressure are high risk. Splitting minimum and enriched phases prevents those risks from forcing advanced semantics into the first slice.

No child Beads are created until this frontier is explicitly activated.

title: Prove a macOS-credible platform seam
description: Before the structured-presentation proof, preserve the accepted Linux-first scope while proving that PTY, process, signal, polling, socket-path, permission, and platform-specific EOF behavior do not shape Orbit core ownership or cross-repository contracts. This is a portability-seam audit and the smallest justified isolation work, not a macOS implementation or support promise.
design:
Start from the accepted Linux candidate and preserve ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 behavior. Inventory every OS-dependent operation before choosing code shape: PTY creation and controlling-terminal setup, child process groups and termination, nonblocking reads and final-output EOF semantics, polling, file-descriptor flags, resize ioctls, signals, user identity, runtime directories, Unix-socket permissions, and stale-socket cleanup. Inspect the exact libc Linux and Apple target definitions plus recorded official Darwin or macOS documentation. Keep terminal authority, semantic input, diagnostic or presentation messages, revision semantics, and future durable state outside the platform boundary. Prefer one small concrete platform seam; do not build a generic backend framework or trait hierarchy for a second implementation that does not exist. Do not implement or claim macOS build, runtime, CI, packaging, or support. If isolation requires a new dependency, material ownership change, or surprising LOC increase, pass the Crate gate and stop for user choice before implementation.

If the inventory shows that the current concrete functions already isolate these semantics, an evidence-only closure with no production refactor is preferable to moving code merely to create a platform module.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline and pre-implementation Reference gate route ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 as preserved or hardened; the Bead creates no macOS behavior contract.
2. The audit maps every current Linux-specific PTY, process, signal, poll, file-descriptor, socket-path, permission, and EOF or error assumption to its owner, core leakage risk, and credible Darwin or macOS replacement shape.
3. Terminal authority, semantic input, client messages, presentation framing and revisions, and future durable state contain no Linux-only value or semantic assumption.
4. OS-specific mechanics remain behind one narrow concrete seam with the smallest justified code shape. No generic portability framework, speculative trait hierarchy, second backend, compatibility layer, or unrelated module split is introduced.
5. Existing Linux unit and subprocess contract checks remain green and prove unchanged ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 behavior after any isolation work.
6. The result records an evidence-backed macOS implementation estimate, remaining blockers, and one portability disposition: neutral, isolated platform dependency, or macOS blocker. It does not claim a macOS build or supported platform.
7. Any dependency or feature change passes the Crate gate before manifest edits and updates docs/CRATES.md with Linux and macOS consequences. Using the existing direct libc shape is also recorded explicitly.
8. A material blocker that would shape the core, cross-repository protocol, durable format, ownership model, or require significant LOC stops for explicit user choice.
9. CHANGELOG.md receives no entry for architecture-only isolation. Any unexpectedly changed accepted user- or consumer-visible behavior is recorded under Unreleased with affected contract IDs and proof revision.
10. Closure evidence records exact sources, ownership and code shape, rejected alternatives, checks, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, limitations, and verification commands.
11. If production, test, or manifest changes touch a proved contract owner or implementation surface, closure reruns the indexed canonical checks and advances ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 to the exact accepted proof-bearing commit, or downgrades each affected contract with its gap. An inventory-only result explicitly retains the existing proof revision and does not claim that audit consumption refreshed it.
notes: Accepted proof revision 2b1a8e3ba4a256c3bdb1018c6dc48a8b089193e0. One concrete src/platform.rs owner around direct libc 0.2.189 encapsulates PTY creation and normalized I/O closure, controlling-terminal and process-group lifecycle, resize and descriptor flags, raw polling and neutral readiness conversion, signals, socket paths, permissions, stale cleanup, and socket identity. src/main.rs retains terminal authority, semantic input, protocol, and processing order without libc or poll-descriptor concepts. Rejected for this proof: generic traits or backends, a second implementation, portable-pty, nix or rustix replacement, Ghostty application or thread architecture, dependency changes, macOS implementation or CI, and protocol changes. Canonical checks passed on the proof revision: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (13); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Owned Rust is 1,554 lines, +68 from the pre-bead baseline: main 579, platform 336, tests 639. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are unchanged. A post-candidate pty-process 0.5.3 scratch build passed the same checks and reduced owned Rust by 44 lines while adding pty-process, rustix, and linux-raw-sys to the normal Linux graph; it remains a credible separate user-approved crate decision, not part of this proof. Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency. A future user-authorized macOS slice is estimated at 0.5 to 1 day and must remove the Linux crate cfg, settle Apple libc compile details, and prove Darwin PTY, process, signal, poll, socket, and cleanup behavior. No macOS behavior is claimed.
close_reason: Accepted platform-seam proof at 2b1a8e3ba4a256c3bdb1018c6dc48a8b089193e0

title: Provide bounded retained-history search
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires the accepted pre-graduation Orbit history contract and a separate user-approved search contract before implementation.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and the accepted history, selection, and copy contracts.
- Orbit owns complete retained-history matching; Venus owns query interaction, result presentation, and ephemeral navigation.

Why:
Search is useful but is not required to prove native history, scrolling, selection, and copy. Keeping it separate prevents an optional indexing and query surface from delaying the minimum usable Eon dogfood path.

Scope:
- Provide bounded literal search over Orbit-retained history through the smallest authoritative libghostty-owned surface.
- Before choosing an algorithm, inspect the exact then-current published safe Rust API, public C API, and underlying Ghostty search implementation. Compare direct public reuse, a small upstream binding addition, a bounded Orbit-owned scan, and no search.
- Define explicit query-byte, direction, case, result-anchor, continuation, cancellation, pruning, epoch-change, pressure, and incomplete-result semantics.
- Add a separately owned Venus consumer that navigates exact authoritative result anchors.

Out of scope:
- Regex, fuzzy or semantic search, indexing service, durable transcript, command database, shell-history integration, cross-session search, agent API, remote search, client-side scanning of unfetched pages, copied Ghostty search code, a private libghostty adapter, or a fork.

Implementation gate:
Activate only after orb-j0m closes, Eon graduation records a go, and orb-bi4.7 selects search as the single next frontier. Split the reference/ownership decision, Orbit owner, Venus consumer, and acceptance work into independently provable children before code.

At activation, use a sufficient public libghostty search API if one exists. Otherwise determine whether a small upstream binding addition removes the complete terminal-search responsibility while preserving bounded synchronous owner-loop work. Implement an Orbit-owned bounded literal scan only after the public and upstream routes are reproducibly unavailable or insufficient. Stop for user choice before a fork, private adapter, substantial wrapper, second terminal parser, or independent history index.
design:
Current discovery evidence, not a future Reference gate: crates.io libghostty-vt and libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1 pin Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. The safe Rust crate exposes no terminal search module or method, and the pinned public C headers expose no search API. The underlying Ghostty terminal/search.zig exports internal Active, PageList, Screen, and Viewport search implementations and states that its search thread is unavailable in libghostty because of the xev dependency. This disproves direct public reuse at 0.2.1 but does not preselect an Orbit scan for a later version.

At activation, rerun the Reference gate against exact current identities. Prefer an existing dependency surface that removes terminal matching, Unicode, wrapping, reflow, and retained-history traversal as one responsibility. A proposed upstream addition must prove a small supported synchronous API; it must not import the unavailable search thread or its event-loop dependency by accident. If that route fails, the local fallback scans only authoritative Orbit/libghostty-retained state, performs bounded work per owner-loop turn, and adds no duplicate transcript or index by default.

Orbit owns query execution, continuation, cancellation, and authoritative anchors. Venus owns native query editing, result display, and ephemeral navigation. Any new crate, feature, fork, wrapper, or persistent index requires its own approved gate. If no shape can provide stable bounded result anchors across the accepted history lifecycle, retain no search rather than inventing a second history owner.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user approves and indexes the search contract before implementation with exact owner, consumer, bounds, cancellation, and failure behavior.
2. Before choosing code shape, the Reference gate inspects exact then-current libghostty safe Rust and C APIs plus underlying Ghostty search machinery, and records direct public reuse, a small upstream binding addition, a bounded local scan, and no search as accepted or rejected with reproducible reasons.
3. A sufficient public libghostty API is reused. If it is absent, a small supported upstream binding addition is evaluated before local matching. Orbit-owned scanning is allowed only after those routes are unavailable or fail the accepted bounds, ownership, portability, or maintenance requirements; no private adapter, fork, copied search engine, second parser, or independent history index is introduced implicitly.
4. Literal matching is correct across Unicode, wrapping, resize and reflow, pruning, alternate-screen policy, detach, reconnect, epoch changes, and session exit.
5. Query length, retained rows scanned, work per turn, result count, continuation state, queued bytes, and cancellation latency are explicitly bounded.
6. Search cannot block PTY processing, live presentation, history interaction, semantic input, effects, or cleanup.
7. Venus receives exact authoritative result anchors and never reconstructs or searches unfetched terminal history.
8. Closure records exact Orbit and Venus proofs, libghostty and Ghostty identities, upstream outcome where attempted, compatibility order, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, performance evidence, and rejected regex, indexing, transcript, agent, private-adapter, and fork scope.

title: Qualify rio-vt as a disposable Orbit engine candidate
description:
## Why

The user selected a bounded rio-vt experiment because its durable evidence is useful whether rio-vt passes, partially fits, or fails. Orbit currently depends on libghostty-vt 0.2.1 and Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. rio-vt may offer lower Rust-side integration friction, more direct terminal-state access, easier Orbit-specific experimentation, and a more approachable basis if Yazelix ever chooses to own a terminal engine. It may instead prove that libghostty's mature terminal semantics and cleaner embedding boundary outweigh Zig and FFI cost.

This task qualifies one exact rio-vt revision against the completed Orbit conformance corpus and records a decision-quality gap matrix. It does not replace libghostty, add a supported engine, or create a permanent dual-engine architecture.

Contract routing:
- Changes no product behavior, ORB-C contract, wire compatibility, proof status, or supported dependency.
- Consumes the exact completed orb-8s0 corpus and evaluates preservation of ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9.
- A candidate pass cannot promote or replace an accepted proof. Adoption requires a separate explicit user decision, contract routing, dependency gate, implementation Bead, and proof lifecycle.

## Evidence

- docs/CRATES.md records libghostty-vt 0.2.1 as the selected authoritative engine, its existing ten-package Rust graph, Ghostty source and Zig build cost, and rio-vt as an unselected replacement candidate.
- docs/REFERENCES.md:188-201 routes rio-vt commit 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 as the strongest Rust-native alternative and rejects librio as a substitute for Orbit's detach boundary.
- rio-vt/Cargo.toml:18-39 keeps corcovado, teletypewriter, simdutf, configuration/search support, and other dependencies non-optional on the normal non-Wasm path. simdutf 0.7.0 builds bundled C++ through cc, so current rio-vt is Cargo-managed but not a strictly Rust-source-only dependency graph.
- rio-vt/src/event/mod.rs:128-288 mixes terminal effects and PTY replies with Rio application commands such as native tabs, fullscreen, quake mode, configuration, window creation, and shutdown.
- rio-vt/src/crosswords/mod.rs:423-463 exposes direct grid, selection, color, title, graphics, cursor, route, working-directory, user-variable, and renderer-notification state. This is powerful for experimentation but creates coupling and API-stability risk.
- rio-vt/README.md:98-127 still requires an EventListener::event method removed from the actual trait at rio-vt/src/event/mod.rs:413-421, confirming churn in the newly extracted embedding surface.
- librio/src/lib.rs:230-335 owns a PTY, terminal machine, I/O thread, and process lifecycle. That shape violates Orbit's sole PTY and owner-loop authority and is excluded.
- include/ghostty/vt/terminal.h:20-109 exposes an opaque caller-driven terminal with synchronous effects and no required PTY, renderer, timer, or background-thread ownership, which currently fits Orbit's boundary.
- At Rio commit 3e41b8b, rio-vt contains about 27,055 Rust code lines and 442 #[test] functions. Its standalone extraction began at a0a7a0e05 on 2026-07-26 and received 43 follow-up commits by the inspected 2026-08-05 revision. The underlying Rio terminal code predates the extraction; the embeddable public seam is new.
- At Ghostty a887df42, src/terminal contains about 89,650 Zig code lines, 2,376 Zig tests, and a substantial parser/OSC fuzz corpus. These counts are maintenance evidence, not directly comparable correctness scores.

## Scope

In scope:
- Qualify one exact rio-vt revision, beginning with 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 unless activation records a newer exact release and preserves comparison with this baseline.
- Feed the orb-8s0 deterministic stimuli into rio-vt and translate only Orbit-owned semantic observations needed by the corpus.
- Measure corpus results, adapter LOC and coupling, dependencies and source languages, build and offline/Nix implications, focused engine throughput and memory under one identical correctness-checked workload, and gaps in state, input, effects, history, selection, graphics, and lifecycle integration.
- Compare four long-term shapes: retain libghostty; retain rio-vt as a benchmark only; pursue bounded upstream rio-vt cleanup then requalify; or recommend a separate adoption/fork decision.
- Preserve exact commands, source identities, adapter patch or recipe, raw measurements, classifications, and negative results as Bead evidence.

Out of scope:
- Using librio, Sugarloaf, Canario, Rio's PTY/event loop/windowing, or another renderer.
- Editing production Orbit code, replacing libghostty, changing Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock without the required gate and user approval, changing ORBS/ORBF, adding a runtime engine trait or feature flag, supporting two engines, publishing a trace format, creating a repository, or shipping candidate code.
- Forking Rio or Ghostty, implementing orbit-vt, upstream issues or pull requests, terminal feature fixes, Venus rendering, end-to-end product benchmarking, or compatibility claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical criteria are stored in this Bead's `acceptance_criteria` field.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Begin only after orb-8s0 is closed with an exact accepted corpus revision and documented command. Claim this Bead and record its Execution baseline before any proof-code, test, manifest, or fixture edit.
2. Complete the Reference gate before proof code. Required: exact accepted Orbit contracts and corpus; rio-vt and librio at 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098; pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1, libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1, Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and their relevant render/effect/input/test surfaces. Rio application, librio PTY, Sugarloaf, and Canario behavior are comparison or rejected scope, not inherited architecture.
3. Pass the Crate gate before any tracked manifest edit. Compare: source-only analysis; a disposable out-of-tree Cargo adapter; the smallest separately approved tracked non-product spike; and no experiment. Default to the out-of-tree adapter. If reproducibility cannot be retained through exact commands and a bounded patch/recipe, stop for user approval before adding a tracked package or workspace member.
4. Use rio-vt directly. Orbit remains the conceptual owner of PTY bytes, terminal-generated reply routing, semantic inputs, presentation extraction, bounds, and lifecycle. Do not instantiate rio-vt performer::Machine or librio Surface.
5. Start with the smallest in-memory engine cases. Add a bounded real-PTY comparison only if a named corpus invariant cannot be evaluated without Orbit's PTY owner. Do not reproduce the broader dogfood or performance baselines.
6. Map every entry in the accepted corpus inventory before execution. Exercise every engine-applicable case. Exclude a case only when its invariant belongs to Orbit's PTY, transport, or lifecycle boundary rather than terminal-engine semantics, recording the exact owner and rationale. Classify each exercised case as pass, equivalent-but-different, missing public surface, unsupported feature, candidate defect, ambiguous expectation, or harness defect. Exact equality applies only to canonical Orbit outputs; do not make libghostty internals the oracle.
7. Inventory every rio-vt type and field the adapter touches. Classify each as stable public API, exposed implementation detail, Rio application coupling, PTY/event-loop coupling, native/C++ dependency, or candidate fork pressure.
8. Measure clean build inputs, Cargo packages, native code/toolchains, offline/Nix requirements, build time, artifact size, adapter code, and one focused identical engine workload. Performance evidence must use the same stimuli, environment, repetitions, correctness oracle, and report a distribution or bound. It cannot claim Venus or end-to-end latency.
9. Evaluate current capabilities explicitly: parser partials; primary/alternate state; pending wrap; Unicode and graphemes; styles/colors/hyperlinks; title/CWD; terminal replies and effects; semantic input; resize/reflow; viewport/history; selection/copy; search; graphics; damage; state export/import. Record that rio-vt's visible VT formatter is not exact checkpoint/restore unless independently disproved.
10. End with exactly one recommendation: reject and retain libghostty; retain rio-vt only as a recurring comparator; request a bounded upstream cleanup and requalify; or ask the user to authorize a separate dependency/fork/adoption decision. Do not implement the recommendation in this Bead.

## Verification

- The completed orb-8s0 command passes unchanged for the accepted libghostty baseline.
- The exact rio-vt adapter command accounts for the complete accepted inventory: it runs every engine-applicable case, records evidence-backed exclusions only for non-engine-owned cases, and emits the classified result table.
- Repeating deterministic cases produces identical results.
- Focused measurements retain their raw samples, environment, correctness result, and summary distribution or bound.
- If any tracked Eon Sessions surface is separately approved, cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, repository governance checks, and git diff --check pass. Otherwise br lint, br sync --flush-only, evidence hashes, and git diff --check cover the planning/evidence surface.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if orb-8s0 lacks an engine-consumable case boundary; report the exact gap without rewriting that Bead in this run.
- Stop if the first useful candidate requires Orbit to surrender PTY, terminal-reply, protocol, lifecycle, or presentation authority.
- Stop if a maintained Rio fork or production abstraction is required before a meaningful corpus pass.
- Stop for explicit user approval before a repository manifest, tracked spike package, fork, binding extension, public artifact, or product contract change.
- Stop if a candidate result would be reported as exact checkpointing, compatibility, performance superiority, or production readiness without direct proof.
- A corpus mismatch is evidence, not authorization to fix Orbit, rio-vt, Ghostty, or libghostty in this task.

Portability disposition: neutral engine stimuli and observations; record Linux build/runtime evidence and macOS/Wasm credibility separately without making support claims.
acceptance_criteria:

2. The experiment pins exact rio-vt, Rio, libghostty-vt, libghostty-vt-sys, and Ghostty identities and records licenses, relevant API maturity, and any source drift from the planning evidence.
3. No product code, ORB-C contract, ORBS/ORBF value, accepted proof, supported engine, production manifest, package, runtime flag, or distribution surface changes.
4. rio-vt is exercised directly without librio, Sugarloaf, Rio windowing, performer::Machine, Rio-owned PTY lifecycle, or a second terminal authority.
5. Every case in the accepted corpus inventory is accounted for. Each engine-applicable case has one classified result: pass, equivalent-but-different, missing public surface, unsupported, candidate defect, ambiguous expectation, or harness defect. An exclusion names the exact non-engine contract owner and rationale. No libghostty-internal behavior is promoted into an Orbit contract.
6. Results cover the accepted engine-sensitive surfaces in ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9, including parser splits, screen transitions, wrap, Unicode, rich cells, replies/effects, input, resize/reflow, viewport/history, selection/copy, and presentation extraction.

notes:
User decision on 2026-08-08: create this experiment because it yields useful durable evidence regardless of candidate outcome. The experiment's product is the corpus result, boundary audit, dependency/build measurement, and gap matrix; candidate adapter code is disposable unless a later explicit decision says otherwise.

The central hypothesis is not that rio-vt is a better terminal today. It is that rio-vt may be better raw material if Yazelix later chooses to own terminal semantics. libghostty remains the default production recommendation while this task is deferred.

Known planning conclusions to preserve:
- rio-vt, not librio, is the only relevant engine candidate for Orbit.
- Rust-native state access, customization, and forkability are rio-vt's plausible unique advantages.
- Current upstream rio-vt does not provide exact checkpoint/restore and is not strictly Rust-source-only because simdutf builds C++.
- libghostty currently has the cleaner Orbit embedding boundary and much deeper conformance/fuzz evidence.
- Direct grid access is both an advantage and a coupling hazard.
- A passing spike is insufficient to justify migration; an independently valuable product requirement or material lifecycle-cost reduction must justify adoption.

Dependency order: orb-8s0 blocks this task. No graduation dependency is modeled because qualification evidence is technically independent; if Orbit receives a no-go and is abandoned, close this task as not applicable.

Rejected alternatives: a librio spike, a permanent backend feature flag, a generic engine trait before a second accepted engine, adopting rio-vt for language aesthetics alone, starting orbit-vt from scratch before measured requirements, or forking before upstream-clean fit is tested.

Planning estimate: effort M, 480 minutes. Implementation risk LOW because production remains untouched; interpretation risk MEDIUM due legitimate terminal-semantic differences; strategic risk HIGH if disposable code is allowed to become a maintained second backend.

title: Upstream erased-row loss for libghostty tracked references
description:
Low-priority external correctness work in Ghostty. This Bead changes no product contract, does not block orb-j0m, and must not create an Orbit fork or private adapter.

Known failure:
External tracked grid references can silently change semantic identity after erased scrollback is removed. CSI 3 J reaches PageList history erasure; affected pins are remapped to retained storage rather than marked garbage. Later output can move the replacement cell into history, allowing an old external reference to resolve to the wrong row.

Outcome:
Confirm the failure against current Ghostty main, obtain the required human contribution access, and propose the smallest upstream correction if maintainers accept the issue. The native Orbit viewport and selection design does not expose long-lived history references, so this work is independent maintenance rather than product-path work.
design:
Exact prior proof:
- Pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 reproduced the clear-and-repopulate semantic remap.
- A disposable candidate changed three Ghostty files by +42/-2; 32 added lines were regression tests and production code was net +8.
- The candidate added an internal Pin.invalidate_on_erase bit, enabled it only for C-created external tracked pins, and marked those pins garbage when their row was erased.
- Internal viewport and selection pins retained existing remapping behavior, Pin remained 16 bytes, and focused tracked-grid-reference tests passed.
- No public C API, Rust wrapper, dependency, or Orbit change was required.

Submission discipline:
Rebase the proof onto current Ghostty before proposing code. Follow current CONTRIBUTING and AI rules exactly: the user writes any vouch request personally, discloses the extent of Codex assistance, and understands every submitted line. Open or obtain an accepted issue before a pull request when policy requires it. Treat the prior patch as evidence, not as a shape maintainers must accept.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Current Ghostty main is checked for the clear-and-repopulate failure with exact revision and focused reproducer.
2. The accepted issue states external tracked-reference semantic loss precisely and does not claim Orbit needs client-side paging.
3. Current contribution and AI rules are followed; the human author writes the vouch request and can explain the patch and tests.
4. Any patch preserves ordinary append and pruning behavior for surviving references, invalidates externally tracked references whose semantic row is erased, and preserves dependency-owned internal viewport and selection behavior.
5. Focused regression tests cover erased-reference loss and unaffected-reference stability; the required upstream checks pass.
6. No public API, new dependency, Orbit fork, private adapter, or libghostty-rs pin change is added unless separately chosen.
7. Closure records the upstream outcome: merged, rejected, superseded, or no longer reproducible. A later Orbit dependency update is a separate user-approved Bead only if the product needs it.
notes: Priority P3 and deferred by user choice on 2026-08-06. Do not activate during the native orb-j0m path.

title: Record VT and Unicode baselines through Orbit and Venus
description:
Cross-repository verification task with no new user-visible behavior, terminal compatibility promise, or product contract. After orb-bi4.6 proves the first composed dogfood path, record one reproducible VT and Unicode baseline through the actual pinned Orbit server, PTY child, ORBS and ORBF bridge, and Venus native renderer.

Use a focused VTTEST scorecard plus ucs-detect and ucs-browser. The purpose is not to re-prove the complete libghostty terminal engine. It is to detect whether terminal modes, replies, input, structured presentation, Unicode cell semantics, glyph shaping, and native rendering survive the boundaries Eon owns.

Contract routing:
- Changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract or proof status by itself.
- Exercises the exact accepted ORB-C2 and ORB-C4 through ORB-C6 boundary, later accepted history and selection contracts where relevant, and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 plus VEN-C7 when accepted. Reconfirm IDs and exact proofs at activation.
- Routes every discrepancy to one Orbit, Venus, Eon, upstream, tool-expectation, or unsupported-capability owner. It repairs none of them.

Out of scope:
- An Eon terminal-emulation profile, xterm compatibility guarantee, exhaustive conformance claim, copied or vendored external suite, esctest integration, upstream libghostty testing, automated screenshot farm, per-push or scheduled CI, product code, protocol changes, new runtime dependencies, performance benchmarking, macOS support, or feature expansion.
design:
Verification plan:

1. Start only after orb-bi4.6 closes with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions and a reproducible composed launch path. Record a planning and evidence baseline; this is a no-code acceptance run unless a minimum local command is later approved as necessary.
2. Pass a Reference and tool gate before tracked test, script, workflow, Nix, fixture, or documentation edits. Required evidence: the exact VTTEST source and release, applicable DEC manuals and xterm control-sequence documentation, the exact ucs-detect and ucs-browser release with its wcwidth and Unicode data identities, exact pinned libghostty and Ghostty behavior, and the accepted Orbit and Venus contracts. Compare focused direct use, esctest, owned synthetic cases, and no external suite. Keep esctest rejected unless a later exact review shows a maintained profile that removes rather than adds expectation ownership.
3. Launch the exact accepted pair through the existing Eon dogfood path. VTTEST and ucs-detect must run as real PTY children owned by Orbit while the real Venus client renders and supplies input. Do not substitute standalone Ghostty, a fake frame source, the diagnostic text client, raw PTY replay, or a handwritten protocol consumer.
4. Select the smallest VTTEST menu set that crosses owned boundaries: cursor movement and save or restore, margins and scrolling regions, erase behavior, SGR and colors, origin and wrap modes, alternate screen where covered, device status and attributes, resize-sensitive behavior, and representative keyboard sequences. Record pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, and not-run outcomes; never report a blanket conformance score.
5. Run ucs-detect with a saved machine-readable report for bounded representative wide, zero-width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. Run ucs-browser visually for alignment and glyph quality using the actual Venus font stack. Distinguish Orbit and libghostty cursor-position or cell-width semantics from Venus shaping, fallback, atlas, and visual alignment.
6. Treat the ucs-detect wcwidth model as one comparator rather than product law. Classify every delta against the exact Unicode versions, accepted libghostty behavior, advertised terminal modes, actual glyph result, and prior Eon baseline. Unsupported graphics or terminal modes are not failures merely because a probe exists.
7. During a focused stateful case, resize once and detach then reattach Venus once to check that the observed state remains coherent across the accepted bridge. Do not repeat the broader lifecycle and application matrix already proved by orb-bi4.6.
8. Record exact Eon manifest and component commits; operating system, display backend, GPU and driver, locale, TERM and capability declarations, geometry, font and fallback stack; tool and Unicode versions; commands, menu items, generated report hashes or locations, screenshots where needed, elapsed time, and every classified result.
9. A regression in a claimed supported capability or an Orbit to Venus boundary invariant blocks closure and names one owner. A tool expectation mismatch or unsupported feature remains recorded evidence. Product fixes, protocol changes, renderer changes, new capabilities, and upstream work require separately authorized owner Beads.
10. The initial baseline is manual Linux evidence. Rerun after relevant libghostty, Unicode, font, shaping, input, presentation, or renderer changes and before releases carrying them. A future accepted macOS client consumes the method in its own platform proof rather than inheriting this Linux result.

Do not add a CHANGELOG entry. README LOC changes only if tracked handwritten verification text is later required; generated logs and screenshots remain evidence artifacts, not product source.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-bi4.6 is closed with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions, and the baseline records the EON-C, ORB-C, and VEN-C implementations exercised without changing or promoting any contract.
2. A pre-edit Reference and tool gate records exact VTTEST, DEC or xterm references, ucs-detect, wcwidth, Unicode data, libghostty, Ghostty, Eon, Orbit, and Venus identities and licenses. It compares direct focused use with esctest, owned synthetic checks, and no external suite.
3. VTTEST and ucs-detect run inside the real Orbit-owned PTY while the real pinned Venus client renders and sends input through canonical ORBS and ORBF. Evidence identifies the actual processes and rejects standalone-emulator or fake-frame substitution.
4. One focused VTTEST scorecard covers the selected cursor, scrolling-region, erase, style or color, origin or wrap, terminal-reply, resize, and keyboard surfaces. Every item is classified as pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, or not run with no blanket xterm or DEC conformance claim.
5. One saved ucs-detect report covers bounded representative width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. One ucs-browser pass visually checks alignment, shaping, fallback, and glyph quality in Venus.
6. Results distinguish authoritative Orbit and libghostty state, replies, and cell semantics from Venus presentation, shaping, fallback, and visual rendering. No client-side terminal model or alternate expectation owner is introduced.
7. One selected stateful result remains coherent across a real resize and Venus detach and reattach. This does not duplicate or replace the orb-bi4.6 application and lifecycle matrix.
8. Every deviation names one exact owner: Orbit, Venus, Eon composition, pinned upstream, external-suite expectation, environment, or explicitly unsupported capability. A regression in accepted behavior blocks closure; no product repair occurs in this Bead.
9. Evidence records exact commits, tools, platform, display, GPU, locale, TERM, geometry, fonts, Unicode data, commands, selected cases, report or screenshot locations, duration, and classified outcomes so a later run can compare deltas.
10. No external test source is copied or vendored; no esctest profile, compatibility layer, runtime dependency, product mode, protocol surface, CI job, schedule, screenshot farm, or full upstream conformance suite is added.
11. The recurring trigger is recorded as after relevant engine, Unicode, shaping, input, presentation, renderer, or platform changes and before releases that carry them. Linux evidence makes no macOS claim.
12. Any tracked planning or minimal verification surface passes governance and git diff checks. Closure records limitations and one result: accepted integration baseline, or held open with one named owner regression.
notes:
User decision on 2026-08-07: adopt well-known VT and Unicode checks from time to time. Use VTTEST plus ucs-detect and ucs-browser through the real stack; avoid duplicating Ghostty upstream conformance ownership.

VTTEST and Unicode checks share this Bead because both require the same exact composed processes, environment capture, native rendering observation, classification model, and cross-repository defect routing. Separate Orbit and Venus test Beads would duplicate setup while neither could prove the full boundary alone.

This Bead intentionally follows orb-bi4.6 rather than blocking first dogfood or graduation. The accepted real-application matrix remains the primary product check. This baseline is periodic hardening before relevant releases and after material terminal or rendering changes.

Rejected defaults: adopting esctest and maintaining an Eon-specific expectation profile; treating Python wcwidth as absolute product truth; importing all upstream Ghostty tests; using vtebench as correctness evidence; automating screenshots; or adding every sanitizer and conformance tool to CI.

Expected implementation risk is LOW. Interpretation risk is MEDIUM because VT behavior and Unicode width contain legitimate versioned or terminal-specific deviations; exact environment capture and owner classification are therefore acceptance requirements.
